dc-multisite.citation: ipSpace.net 'Data Center Interconnects' / 'External Routing with Layer-2 DCI' (Pepelnjak) and 'Choose the Optimal VPN Service' (E-LAN/VPLS usage; stretched-VLAN-DCI 'disaster'); OTV / IETF EVPN

dc-multisite.title: At scale, replace full-mesh inter-site peering with a Route Server, and collapse the Border Gateway onto the spine deliberately
dc-multisite.recommended_action: Deploy redundant Route Servers reachable from every BGW (require EVPN AF, VPN-route reflection, next-hop-unchanged and RT-rewrite; keep them out of the data path); where border leaves are not justified, use spine-as-Anycast-BGW with a Site-ID and per-L2VNI DF election, providing the BGW-to-BGW control path via iBGP to the Route Server, and scale out to up to ~4 A-BGWs per site.
dc-multisite.citation: AJ SDD 'Anycast Border Gateway' / 'BGW on Spine' / 'Route Server' / 'Next Hop unchanged' / 'Route-target rewrite'; corroborated by Cisco VXLAN EVPN Multi-Site design

dc-overlay.title: Restore the BGP L2VPN EVPN control plane before baselining or freezing the overlay fabric
dc-overlay.recommended_action: Work the control plane top-down only after the underlay is confirmed clean. (1) Verify the underlay/loopback reachability the BGP session rides on — a flapping or unreachable spine/RR loopback presents as an EVPN session problem. (2) Run 'show bgp l2vpn evpn summary' on the leaf and its route reflectors/spines; confirm the neighbor is Established and PfxRcd is non-zero. If the session is down, inspect the BGP neighbor state/last-error (AS number, update-source loopback, missing 'address-family l2vpn evpn', RR client config, password/TTL). (3) If the session is up but no routes import, compare route-targets between sites and apply 'rewrite-evpn-rt-asn' where ASN-auto RTs differ; verify Type-2 and Type-3 routes are present with 'show bgp l2vpn evpn'. (4) Re-validate that L2RIB MAC routes are being redistributed into EVPN and that remote VTEPs now see them. For large-scale fabrics, extend BGP graceful-restart (e.g. toward 300s) so a high VNI-count reconvergence does not itself trigger a flap. Only re-snapshot the fabric once EVPN is Established and exchanging routes fabric-wide.
dc-overlay.citation: IETF RFC 7432, BGP MPLS-Based Ethernet VPN (EVPN route types: Type-2 MAC/IP Advertisement, Type-3 Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag; control-plane MAC learning) — corroborated by Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS VXLAN Configuration Guide, Configuring VXLAN BGP EVPN, and Cisco support doc 'Troubleshoot EVPN/VXLAN in Multi-Site Environment' (show bgp l2vpn evpn summary; rewrite-evpn-rt-asn)

dc-overlay.title: Restore the down NVE (VTEP) peer before treating the affected segments as migratable
dc-overlay.recommended_action: Diagnose bottom-up, since the NVE peer is a symptom of the underlay. (1) From 'show nve peers', identify the peer IP (the remote VTEP loopback) and its State. (2) Confirm underlay reachability to that loopback: ping/traceroute the remote VTEP source-interface from this VTEP's source-interface, and verify the /32 is present via the underlay IGP/BGP (route present, correct next-hops, no flaps). (3) Verify both ends' NVE config: 'show nve interface' for the correct 'source-interface loopback', host-reachability protocol bgp, and that the two VTEPs share at least one configured VNI. (4) For vPC VTEPs, confirm the NVE source-loopback hold-down timer is set below the vPC delay-restore timer so the VIP is not advertised before the overlay is ready, and check the anycast/secondary-IP configuration. (5) Once the loopback is reachable and config matches, the peer should transition to Up with LearnType CP; re-verify before clearing the segment for migration.
dc-overlay.citation: IETF RFC 8365, A Network Virtualization Overlay Solution Using EVPN (VTEPs as NVEs depend on IP reachability between NVEs; VXLAN UDP encapsulation; VNI as segment identifier) — corroborated by Cisco support doc 'Configure VXLAN' (118978) and Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS VXLAN Configuration Guide (show nve peers State/LearnType; source-interface loopback; vPC NVE source-loopback hold-down vs delay-restore)

dc-overlay.title: Restore the down NVE VNI (segment) before declaring that L2VNI/L3VNI ready for cutover
dc-overlay.recommended_action: Resolve from the local binding outward. (1) From 'show nve vni' (or 'show nve vni <id> detail'), confirm the VNI's State, Mode (CP), and Type (BD for L2VNI / VRF for L3VNI). (2) For an L2VNI Down: verify the VLAN exists and is active, the VLAN-to-VNI mapping is correct, and a matching 'member vni' is present under the NVE interface; bring the VLAN/bridge-domain up. (3) For an L3VNI Down: verify the tenant VRF, that the L3VNI VLAN/SVI is up and uses 'ip forward', and that 'member vni <id> associate-vrf' is configured — drive state by shut/no-shut on the VRF, never on the VNI interface. (4) Confirm the segment's evidence end-to-end: the VLAN/SVI is up, the VNI shows Up, and EVPN is advertising that VNI's Type-2/Type-3 routes to peers. (5) Only then mark the L2VNI/L3VNI ready and re-baseline that segment.
dc-overlay.citation: Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS VXLAN Configuration Guide, Configure VXLAN / Configure VXLAN BGP EVPN (show nve vni State Up/Down, Type BD vs VRF; VLAN-to-VNI mapping and member vni; L3VNI SVI 'ip forward' and member vni associate-vrf; drive L3VNI via VRF shut/no-shut) — RFC 8365 corroborates VNI-to-broadcast-domain mapping and EVPN carriage of the VNI

dc-services.title: Isolate tenants with per-tenant VRF over a shared L3 core; respect the stateless-ACL TCAM ceiling and the VRF-Lite single-hop limit
dc-services.recommended_action: Map each tenant/zone to its own VRF on the shared core and force all inter-tenant and tenant-to-outside traffic through an explicit policy point; flag any design collapsing distinct zones into one global table as a segmentation gap; where statefulness is not mandated, allow stateless PREFIX-based ACLs with explicit established-session permits and a boundary fragment-drop, but size the ruleset against the switch's published ACL/TCAM capacity and reject per-host rule generation; cap VRF-Lite at single-box/single-hop use and, where isolation must traverse the core, adopt MP-BGP/MPLS-VPN (single-hop PE-PE first) -- or EVPN/VXLAN per-tenant VNIs on an overlay-capable fabric -- so the core stops carrying every VRF's routing.
dc-services.citation: ipSpace.net 'High-Speed Multi-Tenant Isolation' (per-tenant VRF over shared L3; stateless ACL vs stateful FW, established-session match, ToR ACL/TCAM Cartesian explosion, drop fragments); NIL 'Enterprise MPLS/VPN Deployment' ('Multi-VRF Does Not Scale'); RFC 4364

dc-services.title: Model the load balancer as a health-checked VIP-to-pool, choose its insertion mode by return-path and client-IP cost, and don't build LB to mask a non-scale-out app
dc-services.recommended_action: Before committing LB hardware/VIPs, confirm the application is genuinely stateless/scale-out (DB decoupled, no server-pinned session state) and raise a requirement gap if it is scale-up/session-bound rather than masking it in the network; specify the VIP(s), pool membership and the health-probe type/interval per service, preferring an LB (or anycast with route withdrawal) that withdraws failed members over DNS round-robin; choose the insertion mode from return-path and client-IP needs -- Direct Server Return when reverse traffic dwarfs requests, proxy/source-NAT with X-Forwarded-For when full L7 control or the true client IP is needed (documenting that L4-only/IPv6 cases cannot recover the client IP cleanly).
dc-services.citation: ipSpace.net / NIL 'Load Balancing and Scale-Out Application Architectures' (LB principles & operations; transparent vs one-arm; Direct Server Return; X-Forwarded-For; scale-up vs scale-out, decouple-DB prerequisite)

dc-services.title: Anchor firewall/LB at a shared border in its own AS; insert inline services transparently to avoid readdressing
dc-services.recommended_action: Deploy the shared border as a site-external L3-only VTEP in a separate AS with active/standby FW and LB over vPC and centralized route-leaking (dedicated FW-bypass VRF, import-maps denying default leakage, advertise-PIP); for inline service insertion prefer transparent L2 so existing subnets/adjacencies are preserved -- permit the routing hellos across the device, forward ARP/BPDU/non-IP, and use the surviving L3 adjacency as the path-health signal that triggers reroute on appliance failure.
dc-services.citation: AJ SDD 'Shared Border' / 'Shared Border - Firewall' (Centralized Route Leaking, FW-Bypass-VRF) / 'Shared Border - Load Balancer'; ipSpace.net 'High-Speed Multi-Tenant Isolation' (transparent bump-in-the-wire vs routed insertion; routing adjacency as path check)

dc-services.title: Under a distributed anycast gateway, give DHCP relay a unique per-switch loopback GiAddr with Option-82/VNI scope selection
dc-services.recommended_action: Per leaf, assign a unique loopback as the DHCP relay GiAddr and enable Option-82 (dhcp option vpn) scope selection keyed to the L2VNI at the point the gateway is cut to the fabric.
dc-services.citation: AJ SDD 'DHCP RELAY' (Layer 2 Design) -- unique loopback as GiAddr; Option-82 (dhcp option vpn) scope selection by L2VNI

dc-switching.title: Confine each VLAN to a single access switch and consider routed access to shrink oversized L2 domains
dc-switching.recommended_action: Scope each access VLAN to one switch and route between them at distribution; where mobility is genuinely required use an overlay (VXLAN/anycast gateway) rather than a flat stretched VLAN; adopt routed access (with stub access switches + distribution summarization) where VLANs need not span.
dc-switching.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.1 / Session 16 (limit VLAN span, routed access, EIGRP stub + summary); engine vlan_inventory

dc-switching.title: Bind each VLAN to exactly one IP subnet (one-VLAN-one-subnet integrity) before any L2 merge or collapse
dc-switching.recommended_action: For each offending VLAN, choose the authoritative subnet and renumber the others (or split the VLAN per subnet); resolve any containment/mask mismatch so no subnet contains another on the same VLAN; verify one-VLAN-one-subnet before merging or stretching the domain in the target.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco campus/DC L2-L3 design (VLAN<->subnet 1:1, SVI per subnet); RFC 950/1812 subnetting; web-verified.

dc-switching.title: Keep production SVIs out of the platform-reserved VLAN range (e.g. 3968-4095 on Nexus) before migrating to that platform
dc-switching.recommended_action: Renumber each reserved-range SVI into the user VLAN range (1-3967) on both ends before cutover; if the reserved block genuinely must move on the target, schedule the 'system vlan reserve' change + reload in the MOP and validate the SVI comes up.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS Layer-2 Switching Config Guide (VLANs 3968-4095 reserved for internal use); web-verified.

dc-switching.title: Bound the Layer-2 failure domain: a bridged VLAN is one fault domain
dc-switching.recommended_action: Confine each VLAN to the smallest practical span (ideally one access switch / one block); route between blocks at L3 (routed access or a distribution boundary) so an L2 event stays local; prune VLAN 1 and unused VLANs off trunks; where a stretch is unavoidable, isolate it (e.g. a controlled VXLAN/overlay segment with storm-control) rather than raw end-to-end bridging.
dc-switching.citation: ipSpace.net (Pepelnjak) 'A Layer-2 Network Is a Single Failure Domain' / 'The Need for Stretched VLANs'; Cisco CCDA hierarchical-design best practice (no VLAN across multiple access switches)

dc-switching.title: Negotiate multi-member EtherChannels with LACP, not static 'mode on'
dc-switching.recommended_action: Convert each static bundle to LACP (channel-group N mode active on both ends), confirm all members reach 'bundled' (P) state, and leave a single member's failure to suspend rather than blackhole.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco EtherChannel/LACP design (LACP detects miscabling/one-way members that static mode-on admits); web-verified.

dc-switching.title: Use multi-chassis link aggregation (vPC/VSS/SVL/MLAG) so redundant links forward without STP blocking
dc-switching.recommended_action: Configure the aggregation/ToR pair as vPC/VSS/SVL/MLAG and present dual-homed downstreams a single LACP port-channel so both members forward; prefer SVL on Catalyst 9000, migrate legacy VSS to SVL; use an L2 fabric at large scale.
dc-switching.citation: CCDE Session 16 (port-channel/TRILL over STP, vPC/VSS/MLAG); Cisco StackWise Virtual reference 2025

dc-switching.title: Restore N+1 power-supply redundancy before a multi-PSU chassis is silently single-corded
dc-switching.recommended_action: Replace the failed supply to restore N+1; on distribution/core keystones move to dual supplies on independent feeds/grids (2N) and alarm on PSU state; verify both supplies 'OK' before cutover.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco DC platform power design + leading-practice N+1/2N PSU redundancy on aggregation/core; web-verified.

dc-switching.title: Resolve active L2 instability (MAC flapping) before freezing the baseline / cutover
dc-switching.recommended_action: For each flapping host, read the logged VLAN + the two ports, confirm STP state on both (a loop is a link that should be blocking but is forwarding -- resolve the root cause, do not just shut a port), check for a mis-cabled or dual-homed end host bridging two access ports, and rule out a unidirectional link (enable / verify UDLD, check the optic). Clear every active flap and confirm the domain is quiet for a sustained window BEFORE freezing its baseline and scheduling its cutover.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco MAC-flapping / %SW_MATM-4-MACFLAP_NOTIF troubleshooting (L2 loop, dual-homed host, unidirectional link); Cisco STP / UDLD loop-prevention design guidance.

dc-switching.title: Restore degraded EtherChannel / port-channel members (down / suspended / standalone) before cutover
dc-switching.recommended_action: For each degraded bundle, find why the member is not bundling (physical: cabling / SFP / errdisable; config: speed-duplex or LACP/PAgP mode/rate mismatch between the two ends) and restore full membership; verify all members are forwarding before freezing the current-state baseline and scheduling the cutover. In the target, keep LAG min-links / fast-LACP and member monitoring so a future member loss is alarmed, not silent.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco EtherChannel / LACP (IEEE 802.3ad / 802.1AX) member-state troubleshooting (D=down, s=suspended, I=standalone); Cisco port-channel design (min-links, mode/rate match).

dc-switching.title: Adopt spine-leaf (VXLAN-EVPN) for the modern DC; keep collapsed-core+vPC only for small/static footprints
dc-switching.recommended_action: Design the DC as a leaf-spine CLOS with BGP-EVPN overlay (anycast gateway on leaf, endpoints only on leaves, ECMP) and VXLAN-EVPN Multi-Site for DCI; keep collapsed-core+vPC only for small/static DCs.
dc-switching.citation: CCDE Session 16 (spine-leaf); Cisco Nexus 9000 VXLAN BGP EVPN design guide; VXLAN-EVPN Multi-Site WP

dc-switching.title: Engineer a deterministic STP root at distribution, run Rapid-STP, and protect the topology (PortFast/BPDU/Root/Loop Guard, UDLD)
dc-switching.recommended_action: Hard-set primary/secondary root on distribution for every VLAN/MST instance aligned to the active gateway; run Rapid-PVST/RSTP (MST at scale); enable BPDU Guard globally for PortFast edge ports, Root Guard on non-root ports, Loop Guard + UDLD on fibre (aggressive only on dual-homed).
dc-switching.citation: CCDE Session 16 (root at distribution, Rapid STP, BPDU/Root/Loop Guard, UDLD); engine STP parsing

dc-switching.title: Engineer an explicit STP root priority on every active VLAN -- never let the root be elected by the MAC tiebreak
dc-switching.recommended_action: Configure 'spanning-tree vlan X root primary' on the intended root (priority 24576) and 'root secondary' (28672) on its peer, co-located with the active FHRP gateway, for every production VLAN; re-verify after introducing any new switch in the migration.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco STP design (default bridge priority 32768, lowest-MAC tiebreak, explicit root primary/secondary); web-verified.

dc-switching.title: Use a three-tier hierarchy for scale (or full-mesh the distribution if collapsing the core), and tier for blast-radius + RBAC
dc-switching.recommended_action: Introduce a dedicated fast core so distribution blocks attach and scale by addition; if core-less, fully mesh the distribution with root/FHRP there; tier the network (with per-tier flooding domains and summarization) to bound blast radius and align RBAC.
dc-switching.citation: CCDE Session 16 (3 tiers = scalability, full-mesh distribution if no core); CCDE scenario (tiering = blast radius + RBAC)

dc-switching.title: Reconcile vPC / MLAG peer-fabric health (down* legs + consistency mismatches) before cutover
dc-switching.recommended_action: For each down* member vPC, find why it is not bundling on one or both peers (downstream device down, port-channel member fault, or an admin-down leg) and either restore it or record it as intentionally single-attached; clear every type-1 (must-match) and type-2 consistency mismatch so the peers agree; confirm peer-link, keepalive and peer-adjacency are healthy on every domain. Verify each dual-homed device has BOTH legs 'up' before freezing the baseline. In the target, keep peer-link + keepalive monitored and a consistency-check alarm so a future drift is alarmed, not silent.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco NX-OS vPC design & troubleshooting (peer-link / peer-keepalive, type-1/type-2 consistency, 'down*' member state); Cisco multi-chassis (vPC / VSS / MLAG) HA design guidance.

dc-switching.title: Treat active storm-control suppression as a live broadcast storm and find its source before cutover
dc-switching.recommended_action: (1) Confirm and scope the live event: 'show storm-control' and interface counters to identify the affected port(s), the traffic class being suppressed, and whether it is sustained or bursty; correlate with the syslog storm-control messages for onset time. (2) Hunt the source as a loop first — verify STP topology and root, check for ports that should have BPDU guard/portfast but do not, and look for two access ports bridging the same segment; a sudden multi-port broadcast spike is a loop until proven otherwise. (3) If not a loop, localize the talker: identify the MAC/host generating the flood (mis-teamed NIC, chatty multicast app, malware) and isolate or remediate it at source. (4) Validate that the suppression clears (traffic falls below the falling threshold and the port resumes forwarding the class) and that dependent broadcast/multicast services on the VLAN recover. (5) Only after the storm source is eliminated and suppression has cleared should the segment be considered cutover-ready; do not merely raise the threshold to silence the alarm.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco — Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS Security Configuration Guide: Configuring Traffic Storm Control (rising/falling thresholds; once the level is reached, traffic is dropped until the interval ends)

dc-switching.title: Enable IGMP/MLD snooping with a querier and group limits, and insert load-balancing at DC aggregation
dc-switching.recommended_action: Enable IGMP/MLD snooping on multicast VLANs with a querier per active VLAN and per-interface group-join limits; deploy load-balancing/ADC as a redundant pair at the DC aggregation layer with health-check and persistence.
dc-switching.citation: CCDE Session 16 (IGMP snooping/limits, ADC at aggregation); engine build_igmp_queriers

dc-switching.title: Size each VLAN's subnet to its endpoint count -- a VLAN with >254 endpoints cannot live in a /24
dc-switching.recommended_action: Size each oversized VLAN's target prefix to its endpoint count plus headroom (/23 or /22), or split the broadcast domain into multiple VLANs/subnets to bound the failure domain; reflect the choice in the addressing plan.
dc-switching.citation: IPv4 subnetting (/24 = 254 usable hosts) + Cisco fault-domain sizing (bound the broadcast domain); web-verified.

dc-switching.title: Move per-VLAN spanning tree (Rapid-PVST) to MST at high VLAN scale -- one STP instance per VLAN does not scale
dc-switching.recommended_action: Migrate the per-VLAN STP estate to MST: define a small set of MST instances with an explicit VLAN-to-instance map, align the region name/revision/map fleet-wide (a mismatched region silently splits the domain), place per-instance roots deterministically at the distribution, and keep edge protection (BPDU guard / PortFast). In the EVPN/VXLAN target this concern disappears at the fabric (L2 is bounded to the leaf) -- MST is the interim remedy for the brownfield tier.
dc-switching.citation: IEEE 802.1s (Multiple Spanning Tree) / 802.1Q-2014; Cisco campus STP design guidance (Rapid-PVST vs MST at VLAN scale)

dc-switching.title: Size capacity from measured traffic and concurrency -- average utilization is not health, and microbursts drop below 70%
dc-switching.recommended_action: Base link sizes on 95th-percentile edge-port utilization x port count x growth, plus summed real-time session bandwidth; look at egress discards/drops and TCP retransmit ratios (not just utilization) to find congestion; apply QoS to protect real-time and police abusive flows rather than enlarging buffers; size for the busy period and for the service level required DURING a failure.
dc-switching.citation: ipSpace.net / NetCraftsmen 'Sizing the Network' (Terry Slattery) -- 95th-percentile & concurrent-endpoint sizing, microbursts below 70% average, bufferbloat, Mathis-equation loss sensitivity; Cisco WAN capacity-planning white paper

dc-switching.title: Confirm the storm-control action and recovery policy on edge ports before cutover, so a storm fails predictably
dc-switching.recommended_action: (1) Inventory the per-port action and threshold ('show storm-control', 'show running-config interface') and reconcile to intent — access/host edge ports generally warrant tight broadcast suppression (commonly low single-digit percent to cover ARP) with a containment action, uplinks/trunks generally should not carry an aggressive shutdown that could isolate a whole downstream tree. (2) Decide the recovery model explicitly: if 'shutdown' is used, pair it with 'errdisable recovery cause storm-control' and a sane recovery interval so a transient storm self-heals; if a port must never auto-restore (a known-abusive segment), keep manual recovery but document the runbook step. (3) Check 'show errdisable recovery' to confirm the cause is actually enabled and the interval is set. (4) Before the window, identify which edge ports could be transiently storm-tripped by the planned change and pre-stage the recovery (or temporarily relax to 'trap') so the change itself does not err-disable production access. (5) Re-baseline after cutover that no port sits err-disabled by storm-control.
dc-switching.citation: Cisco — Configuring Port-Based Traffic Control: Storm Control (action shutdown=err-disable / trap; recover via shut-no shut or 'errdisable recovery cause storm-control')

dc-switching.title: Consolidate LAN and storage onto one lossless Ethernet fabric only with DCB and a stable L2 -- it merges two failure domains
dc-switching.recommended_action: Where adapter/cable/port reduction justifies it, converge LAN and storage onto a single 10GE+ fabric using FCoE (with DCB/PFC for lossless behaviour) or IP storage (iSCSI/NFS); insist on a stable, loop-controlled underlay (minimize spanning tree, prefer multipath) because storage cannot absorb LAN-style instability; budget and protect a storage QoS class end-to-end; keep the converged-fabric blast radius in mind since LAN and SAN now share a failure domain.
dc-switching.citation: ipSpace.net 'Data Center 3.0 for Networking Engineers' / 'Server Virtualization Overview' (Pepelnjak); Cisco unified-fabric / FCoE design guidance

ddi-ipam.title: Build the IPAM addressing plan as a topology-aligned, summarizable CIDR/VLSM hierarchy (region -> site -> tier) so it aggregates at every routing boundary
ddi-ipam.recommended_action: When authoring/target-state addressing, structure the IPAM plan as contiguous nibble-or-CIDR-aligned parent blocks per region and site that summarize at aggregation boundaries, VLSM-size each segment to its host count, reserve static/infrastructure ranges out of DHCP scopes, and prefer re-addressing scattered legacy subnets into the hierarchy over porting a non-summarizable scatter. (Doctrine: the engine can observe current subnet scatter but cannot derive the intended region/site hierarchy or growth target — those are uncollected business inputs.)
ddi-ipam.citation: RFC 4632 (obsoletes RFC 1519) 'Classless Inter-domain Routing (CIDR): The Internet Address Assignment and Aggregation Plan'; RFC 1518 'An Architecture for IP Address Allocation with CIDR'

ddi-ipam.title: Choose the DHCP server-redundancy model deliberately -- stateful failover/HA over split-scope -- and verify DHCPv6 has its own (RFC 8156) story
ddi-ipam.recommended_action: In the target-state addressing/DDI design, specify the DHCP redundancy model explicitly (failover/HA pair vs split-scope), the mode (load-balancing vs hot-standby) and MCLT, and confirm the chosen server platform provides DHCPv6 failover for every dual-stack scope -- not just DHCPv4. Avoid split-scope where pool utilization is high.
ddi-ipam.citation: RFC 8156 'DHCPv6 Failover Protocol' & RFC 7031 'DHCPv6 Failover Requirements'; RFC 3074 'DHC Load Balancing Algorithm'; ISC KB 'Kea High Availability vs. ISC DHCP Failover'

ddi-ipam.title: Couple the anycast service advertisement to a real service health check (route health injection) and damp advertise/withdraw oscillation
ddi-ipam.recommended_action: (Design) Specify, per anycast service, a health-injection contract: an application-level probe (functional DNS/NTP/AAA transaction, not just port/loopback liveness) that gates the route advertisement via the routing daemon (BIRD/FRR conditional advertise, or interface/next-hop tracking), withdraw-on-failure semantics, a minimum re-advertise dwell timer to prevent rapid oscillation, and origin-proximate flap-dampening of the service prefix. Call out monitoring that is per-instance (observed availability varies by client location, so a single external probe can look healthy while a regional instance black-holes).
ddi-ipam.citation: IETF RFC 4786 / BCP 126 'Operation of Anycast Services' (sec. 4.4.1 availability triggers advertisement / non-availability triggers withdrawal + minimum re-advertise delay; sec. 4.4.4 origin-proximate flap-dampening; client-location availability caveat)

ddi-ipam.title: Front critical infrastructure services (DNS/NTP/AAA) on a service anycast VIP, scoped local-IGP inside the site and global-BGP only across sites
ddi-ipam.recommended_action: (Design) Define a target-state services-addressing plan: a dedicated anycast /32 (and /128) per critical service, advertised from >=2-4 instances; specify IGP-scoped anycast within each site (host route, no summarization that would swallow or mask the /32) and reserve BGP for the inter-site/global scope with a filter-surviving advertisement and an explicit Local->Global failover order. Migrate clients/DHCP options to the anycast VIP rather than per-server unicast IPs. Document the service prefix(es) as protected host routes that must never be aggregated away at the distribution/core boundary.
ddi-ipam.citation: IETF RFC 4786 / BCP 126 'Operation of Anycast Services' (sec. 4.2-4.3 local-IGP vs global-BGP scope, host route vs covering prefix); RFC 3258 'Distributing Authoritative Name Servers via Shared Unicast Addresses'; RFC 9199 'Considerations for Large Authoritative DNS Server Operators'

ddi-ipam.title: Give every endpoint-bearing subnet a redundant DHCP path: dual relay destinations + a server-failover backend, never one helper
ddi-ipam.recommended_action: From the collected relay configuration, count distinct DHCP relay destinations (ip helper-address / forwarding targets) per gateway SVI; cross-reference against endpoint-bearing VLANs. Flag endpoint-bearing subnets whose gateway has 0 relay destinations (DHCP black-hole risk) as Critical/High and those with exactly 1 (no DHCP redundancy) as Medium, citing the specific SVI/VLAN. Recommend a second relay destination plus a failover/HA pairing on the server side.
ddi-ipam.citation: Cisco IOS IP Addressing: DHCP Configuration Guide -- DHCP Relay Agent (multiple 'ip helper-address' forwards a copy to each server); ipSpace.net 'DHCP Relaying with Redundant DHCP Servers'

ddi-ipam.title: Make the relay path FHRP-aware and the snooping/Option-82 trust boundary coherent, so the gateway pair does not double-relay or drop legitimate DHCP
ddi-ipam.recommended_action: In the relay design, specify FHRP-aware DHCP relay on redundant gateways (active-only relay with a deterministic source/return path) rather than independent helper-addresses on both peers; and define one Option-82 trust policy end-to-end -- snooping trusted/untrusted port roles at the access edge reconciled with 'relay information trust-all/trusted' and the server's Option-82 handling -- so legitimate requests are neither duplicated nor dropped.
ddi-ipam.citation: Cisco IOS 'HSRP-Aware DHCP Relay' and 'DHCP Relay Server ID Override and Link Selection (Option 82) Suboptions' configuration guides; Cisco DHCP Snooping configuration guide (Option-82 trusted/untrusted ports, 'ip dhcp relay information trusted')

evpn.title: Keep every Arista BGP-EVPN overlay peer Established (the VXLAN fabric control plane)
evpn.recommended_action: Restore the EVPN peering to Established: verify the session is administratively up, the remote AS / update-source / BGP router-id are correct, the l2vpn evpn address-family is activated for the neighbour, and the route reflectors are reachable; confirm before the fabric is on the cutover path.
evpn.citation: Arista EOS User Manual (EVPN Overview / Configuring EVPN); Arista Network Test Automation (ANTA) BGP / EVPN health tests; analogous to the Cisco NX-OS VXLAN BGP-EVPN (L2VPN EVPN) control plane

evpn.title: Keep every Arista MLAG domain active, connected and config-consistent (the vPC-equivalent dual-active primitive)
evpn.recommended_action: Reconcile the peer configuration until 'show mlag config-sanity' is consistent, confirm the peer-link and member-port state, and restore the domain to active + connected + consistent before the pair is on the cutover path. Treat 'mlag' in the running-config as intent, not proof -- verify the operational state.
evpn.citation: Arista EOS User Manual (Multi-Chassis Link Aggregation); Arista Network Test Automation (ANTA) MLAG health tests (VerifyMlagStatus / VerifyMlagConfigSanity / VerifyMlagInterfaces); analogous to the Cisco Nexus vPC consistency model

evpn.title: Use standards-based EVPN ESI all-active multihoming, not proprietary MC-LAG/vPC, to drop the peer-link and the two-chassis ceiling
evpn.recommended_action: Specify EVPN ESI-based all-active multihoming (auto-derived or manual ESI, advertised via the Ethernet-Segment route) for dual/multi-attached endpoints; reserve single-active per-service mode for cases where the CE cannot run a single LACP bundle across PEs.
evpn.citation: RFC 7432 (BGP-MPLS-Based EVPN) §8 Multi-Homing Functions -- Type-4 Ethernet-Segment + Type-1 Ethernet A-D routes, ESI, aliasing, DF election; web-verified against RFC 7432.

evpn.title: Bound EVPN MAC mobility with the RT-2 sequence number, and arm duplicate-MAC freeze (N moves / M seconds) so a misconfig loop cannot melt the control plane
evpn.recommended_action: Specify in the target-state HLD/LLD that EVPN duplicate-MAC / host-mobility detection is enabled with explicit thresholds (RFC 7432 / Cisco NX-OS default = 5 moves in 180 s, 30 s hold-down, freeze after 5 hold-downs in 24 h), that the static/sticky flag is set on anycast-gateway and other fixed MACs, and that an operational runbook exists to locate and clear a frozen/duplicate MAC. This is target-architecture doctrine: the brownfield engine collects no live EVPN host-mobility-manager state, so it cannot be auto-verified.
evpn.citation: IETF RFC 7432 (BGP MPLS-Based Ethernet VPN) Section 15 / 15.1 'Duplicate MAC Detection' (recommended defaults N=5, M=180s); Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS VXLAN BGP EVPN Configuration Guide (host-mobility-manager move-count / freeze-time / retry-count)

evpn.title: Make all-active multihoming loop-free and duplicate-free with designated-forwarder election plus a split-horizon segment label
evpn.recommended_action: Specify per-EVI DF election and per-segment split-horizon filtering for every multihomed Ethernet Segment; rely on segment auto-discovery (ES-import-filtered) for peer agreement; and explicitly set/justify the peering and recovery timers that govern BUM forwarding during failover.
evpn.citation: RFC 7432 (Route-Type 4 Ethernet-Segment = DF election; split-horizon/ESI label) + native EVPN deep-dive (DF Election / Split-Horizon / Aliasing); web-verified against RFC 7432.

evpn.title: Choose the EVPN DF-election algorithm deliberately (default mod-N vs HRW vs preference-based) and control preemption
evpn.recommended_action: In the HLD, state the chosen DF-election algorithm per Ethernet Segment and justify it: HRW for deterministic minimal-churn behaviour by default; preference-based when DF placement must be operator-pinned, with non-revertive (no-preempt) selected so a recovered PE does not preempt and re-disrupt traffic during a maintenance return. Mandate that every PE on a shared ES is provisioned with the identical algorithm and capability set, and that maintenance runbooks lower preference (or use DF-election timers) to drain a PE gracefully rather than yanking the link.
evpn.citation: IETF RFC 8584 (Framework for EVPN Designated Forwarder Election Extensibility, incl. the HRW algorithm) and RFC 9785 (Preference-Based EVPN Designated Forwarder Election, June 2025 -- Highest-Preference algorithm + Non-Revertive capability, updating RFC 8584)

evpn.title: Decide RT-2 host-route vs RT-5 prefix advertisement deliberately -- decouple IP-from-MAC for floating/silent endpoints, and design coexistence preference so the same host isn't learned twice
evpn.recommended_action: In the target-state design, document the RT-2-vs-RT-5 advertisement policy per VRF/VNI (host-route granularity only where suppression/mobility is needed; RT-5 prefixes for L3VNI, floating IPs, and external reach), align MAC-aging/ARP-refresh timers to prevent silent-host route withdrawal, and pin the RT-2/RT-5 coexistence preference. Target-architecture doctrine -- not auto-verifiable, as the engine collects no EVPN route-type advertisement state.
evpn.citation: IETF RFC 9136 (IP Prefix Advertisement in EVPN, the RT-5 route); RFC 7432 Section 7 (RT-2 MAC/IP Advertisement); Juniper 'EVPN Type 2 and Type 5 Route Coexistence with EVPN-VXLAN' (coexistence preference algorithm); Arista 'EVPN Type-5 Routes: IP Prefix Advertisement'

evpn.title: Engineer the Ethernet Segment identity: one consistent ESI + shared LACP system-ID across the multihoming PE pair
evpn.recommended_action: In the LLD, define the ESI allocation scheme: one unique, stable ESI per Ethernet Segment, identical on both PEs of the pair; the same LACP system-ID/system-MAC on the CE-facing bundle of both PEs; and a different ESI/system-ID for every other segment. Prefer auto-LACP ESI derivation over hand-assigned ESIs to eliminate cross-leaf coordination error, and record the ESI-to-segment map as part of the build sheet so it is auditable at NRFU.
evpn.citation: Juniper EVPN-LAG Multihoming guide (ESI Types & LACP -- same ESI and LACP system-id on all LAG member links) and Cisco NX-OS VXLAN EVPN multihoming guidance (Type-0x03 MAC-based ESI auto-derived from LACP system-id + port-channel key; identical system-MAC across PEs sharing an ESI)

evpn.title: Gate EVPN Type-5 ingress: import only intended external prefixes / a default into each tenant VRF, never an unfiltered route-leak across the border
evpn.recommended_action: For each tenant VRF, specify the Type-5 import policy at the border: which external prefixes (or default-only) are admitted, an explicit inbound route-policy on the untrusted WAN peer, and confirmation that admitted external reachability routes through the intended security/inspection path rather than bypassing it.
evpn.citation: Cisco 'Nexus 9000 VXLAN BGP EVPN ... Fundamental Design and Implementation Guide' (Type-5 origination/import in the tenant VRF, cisco.com); Juniper 'EVPN Type-2 and Type-5 Route Coexistence with EVPN-VXLAN' (junos type-5 ip-prefix-routes import discipline)

evpn.title: Leak between tenant VRFs only through controlled RT import/export (RFC 9136 IP-VRF-to-VRF), never an ad-hoc fusion router
evpn.recommended_action: For shared-services or inter-tenant reachability, design scoped RT export of the shared prefixes into consumer VRFs and import of consumer return routes into the shared VRF (per-prefix, not full-table); document the leak matrix as the source of truth and avoid fusion-router workarounds; if a firewall is inserted, keep the path symmetric.
evpn.citation: RFC 9136 (IP Prefix Advertisement in EVPN, IP-VRF-to-VRF models); Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS VXLAN Configuration Guide -- External VRF Connectivity and Route Leaking / Centralized VRF Route-Leaking for VXLAN BGP-EVPN

evpn.title: Make the VRF-to-L3VNI mapping a single fleet-wide invariant -- a per-VTEP mismatch silently black-holes inter-subnet routing
evpn.recommended_action: Define one canonical per-tenant VRF->L3VNI->route-target mapping and render it identically to all participating VTEPs from automation/SoT; add a pre-cutover conformance check that the mapping is present and identical on every leaf carrying the tenant, and that no L3VNI reuses an L2VNI ID.
evpn.citation: RFC 9135 / RFC 9136 (IP-VRF-to-VRF model, consistent L3VNI requirement); Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS VXLAN Configuration Guide (External VRF Connectivity & Route Leaking)

evpn.title: Stand up the EVPN Type-1 fast-convergence plane: per-EVI Aliasing for load-share, per-ES Mass-Withdrawal for sub-second failover
evpn.recommended_action: In the HLD/LLD convergence section, require both EAD route families on every multihomed segment: per-EVI EAD (Aliasing) for all-active load distribution and per-ES EAD (Mass-Withdrawal) for fast failover, plus the Single-Active backup-path bit where single-active is chosen. Make NRFU assert that per-ES and per-EVI Type-1 routes are present and that a link-down on one PE converges via mass-withdrawal (one update) rather than by MAC aging -- and tie this to the application's stated convergence-time requirement.
evpn.citation: IETF RFC 7432 (Ethernet A-D per-EVI = Aliasing; Ethernet A-D per-ES = Mass-Withdrawal) and Cisco IOS-XR / IOS-XE EVPN Multihoming configuration guides (per-EVI Aliasing load-balancing, per-ES Mass-Withdrawal fast convergence, Single-Active backup path)

evpn.title: Suppress fabric host-routes (/32, /128) at the EVPN border and summarize external prefixes inbound -- the border is a route-scale firebreak
evpn.recommended_action: Design an explicit border route-policy in both directions: outbound filter/summarize so fabric host-routes (/32,/128) are not leaked to the WAN; inbound summarize external prefixes (or inject a default) before they become Type-5 in the fabric. State the leaf route-scale and WAN-table-size budgets the policy protects.
evpn.citation: Cisco 'Nexus 9000 VXLAN BGP EVPN Data Center Fabrics Fundamental Design and Implementation Guide' and 'VXLAN Network with MP-BGP EVPN Control Plane Design Guide' (cisco.com) -- host-route suppression and external-route summarization at the border

evpn.title: Terminate VXLAN-EVPN external L3 at a dedicated border (leaf or spine) over per-VRF VRF-lite handoff, originating Type-5
evpn.recommended_action: In the HLD/LLD name the external-connectivity boundary explicitly: which nodes are border (leaf vs spine and why), the per-tenant-VRF VRF-lite sub-interface/routing-session plan to the edge router, and the requirement that external prefixes re-enter the fabric as Type-5. Do not scatter external peering across compute leaves.
evpn.citation: Cisco 'Nexus 9000 VXLAN BGP EVPN Data Center Fabrics Fundamental Design and Implementation Guide' and 'VXLAN Network with MP-BGP EVPN Control Plane Design Guide' (cisco.com); Cisco IOS-XE 'Configuring EVPN VXLAN External Connectivity' (Catalyst 9000)

igp.title: Authenticate IGP adjacencies and use the overload bit / startup hygiene on restart
igp.recommended_action: Enable IGP neighbour authentication everywhere (HMAC-MD5 IS-IS, SHA-256 EIGRP/keychains); set the IS-IS overload bit (or wait-for-BGP) on restarting/maintenance nodes.
igp.citation: CCDE Session 1/3 (IS-IS HMAC-MD5/overload bit, EIGRP SHA-256)

igp.title: Map the IGP area/level hierarchy onto the core/distribution/access tiers
igp.recommended_action: Introduce a hierarchical IGP: backbone in the core, area/level borders on the distribution-to-core edge, access in stub areas/IS-IS L1; place ABRs on core or DC-border nodes so the backbone stays small.
igp.citation: CCDE Session 1/2 (IS-IS 3-layer, OSPF ABR placement); CCDE scenario (ABR at DC border)

igp.title: Default to a link-state IGP; reserve distance-vector for specific niches
igp.recommended_action: Adopt OSPF or IS-IS as the strategic core/campus IGP with a defined area/level hierarchy; keep EIGRP only for hub-and-spoke edges/stubs where it fits.
igp.citation: CCDE Session 4 (IGP comparison) Link-State vs Distance-Vector; engine routing-protocol inventory

igp.title: Layer BFD detection with pre-computed LFA/TI-LFA backups, matched to topology
igp.recommended_action: Enable BFD for sub-second detection, then select FRR by topology (TI-LFA as the SR-era default incl. rings; classic LFA only where a loop-free alternate is guaranteed); engineer EIGRP feasible-successors and mark spokes as stubs to contain queries.
igp.citation: CCDE Session 1/2/3 (LFA/RLFA/TI-LFA, feasible-successor, SIA/stub); CCDE scenario (Directed-LFA fails on rings -> TI-LFA)

igp.title: Use NSF/SSO and NSR/GR for control-plane HA during supervisor switchover and upgrades
igp.recommended_action: Enable NSF/SSO (with CEF) and NSR/GR for the IGP/BGP/LDP on redundant-control-plane nodes; verify adjacent-router GR support and hold-timer compatibility before enabling GR at the edge.

igp.title: Use stub / totally-stubby / NSSA area types to shrink edge databases, and verify default-route reachability
igp.recommended_action: Make leaf areas stub/totally-stubby (ABR injects only a default); use NSSA where the area must originate externals; explicitly originate the default from the ABR/ASBR and verify reachability after any area-type change.
igp.citation: CCDE Session 2/4 (stub/NSSA); CCDE scenario (Totally-NSSA then NSSA + Type-3 leak; NSSA default-route break)

ipv6.title: Build a deterministic nibble-aligned IPv6 plan from a /48, hold every host subnet at /64, and delegate downstream with DHCPv6-PD
ipv6.recommended_action: Obtain a /48 per site (/44-/40 for large multi-region orgs); reserve nibble-aligned blocks per region->site->role->VLAN; allocate host/access subnets as /64 only; align summary boundaries to aggregation; use DHCPv6-PD for downstream sub-prefix delegation.

ipv6.title: Resolve the duplicate IPv6 address (and free the DUPLICATE-state interface) before baselining the fabric
ipv6.recommended_action: 1) Identify the offending address and scope with 'show ipv6 interface <intf>' (look for DUPLICATE/dadfailed and whether it is the link-local or a global/anycast address). 2) Find the true owner of the address on the link — check the neighbor table / ND cache and the L2 path (MAC behind the solicited-node multicast); on a switched segment trace the duplicate to a second device or a mis-bridged VLAN rather than assuming a stack glitch. 3) Fix the root cause, not the symptom: correct the typo'd static address, remove the duplicate from whichever device is the imposter, or (for an EUI-64/link-local collision from a cloned MAC or VM) re-base the interface identifier. 4) Only after the conflict is genuinely gone, return the address to service — on IOS-XR/IOS-XE clear the latched state with 'clear ipv6 duplicate-address <interface>' (or shut/no-shut, which re-runs DAD), since the DUPLICATE flag does not self-heal once set. 5) Re-verify with 'show ipv6 interface' that the address is now VALID/up and confirm the dependent routing adjacency re-forms. Tune 'ipv6 nd dad attempts' only as a deliberate design choice (e.g. set to 0 on a known-clean point-to-point link), never as a way to mask a real collision.
ipv6.citation: IETF RFC 4862, IPv6 Stateless Address Autoconfiguration, §5.4 Duplicate Address Detection (esp. 5.4.4 'When Duplicate Address Detection Fails' / 5.4.5), and Cisco IOS-XR IP Addresses and Services Command Reference, 'clear ipv6 duplicate-address' / DUPLICATE-state behavior

ipv6.title: Enable the full IPv6 first-hop security suite at the access edge -- RA-Guard, DHCPv6-Guard, ND inspection/device-tracking, IPv6 Source Guard
ipv6.recommended_action: On every host-facing access port enable RA-Guard + DHCPv6-Guard (only real uplinks trusted), enable IPv6 ND inspection / device-tracking to build the binding table, then layer IPv6 Source Guard off that table; apply even on IPv4-only segments where hosts are IPv6-capable (block rogue RAs).
ipv6.citation: Cisco IPv6 First-Hop Security (RA-Guard, DHCPv6-Guard, ND inspection, Source Guard); RFC 6104; web-verified.

ipv6.title: Pick the host-config model per RA M/O flags (design for the Android no-DHCPv6 reality); default to GUA end-to-end, ULA only as a stable adjunct -- never NAT
ipv6.recommended_action: For mixed-OS/BYOD/wireless use SLAAC (A=1) + stateless DHCPv6 (O=1) for DNS; reserve stateful DHCPv6 (M=1) for managed Android-free segments; default to GUA end-to-end secured by stateful firewall/ACLs (no NAT); add ULA only where renumber-independence / hard-offline-internal is required.
ipv6.citation: IPv6 SLAAC (RFC 4862) / DHCPv6 (RFC 8415) / ULA (RFC 4193) design; web-verified (Android no-DHCPv6).

ipv6.title: Restore the down IPv6 routing adjacency before freezing the routing baseline
ipv6.recommended_action: 1) Read the exact stuck state first — 'show ospfv3 neighbor' / 'show ipv6 ospf neighbor' or 'show bgp ipv6 unicast summary' — because the state names the failing phase (INIT/EXSTART vs Idle/Active) and points straight at the cause. 2) Confirm L1-L3 underneath: interface up, and for IPv6 that the link-local is present and NOT in DUPLICATE state (a DAD failure on fe80:: silently kills OSPFv3/EIGRPv6 adjacency); for BGP, ping the peer's IPv6 address and confirm a route to it exists. 3) For OSPFv3 stuck in EXSTART/Exchange, check MTU on both ends first (the highest-yield cause), then reconcile hello/dead intervals, area ID, area type, and authentication; verify no ACL is dropping IP protocol 89. 4) For BGP stuck in Active/Idle, test TCP/179 reachability (telnet to 179) to separate an ACL/firewall/CoPP block from a routing problem, then verify remote-AS, 'update-source' (loopback peering), 'ebgp-multihop'/TTL for multihop eBGP, and any MD5/TCP-AO password. 5) Fix the one mismatched attribute, watch the neighbor walk to FULL / Established, and confirm the expected prefixes are now installed before clearing the cutover gate. Use 'debug ipv6 ospf adj'/'debug ipv6 ospf hello' or 'debug bgp ipv6 unicast' only to confirm a hypothesis, never as the first step on a production box.
ipv6.citation: Cisco, 'Troubleshoot OSPF Neighbor Problems' (Doc ID 13699) and 'Troubleshoot OSPF Neighbors Stuck in Exstart/Exchange State' (Doc ID 13684), plus 'Troubleshoot BGP Neighborship Connection Issues' (Doc ID 13752); RFC 5340 (OSPFv3) for link-local-sourced adjacency

ipv6.title: Choose the coexistence model deliberately: dual-stack to de-risk, then IPv6-mostly (NAT64/DNS64/464XLAT, PREF64, DHCPv4 Option 108) to retire IPv4 at the edge
ipv6.recommended_action: Start dual-stack to de-risk; then move user/wireless segments to IPv6-mostly with NAT64+DNS64, PREF64 advertised in RAs, and DHCPv4 Option 108 for CLAT/464XLAT clients; keep IPv4 only where dependencies require it, behind the translator.
ipv6.citation: IPv6 transition (NAT64/DNS64 RFC 6146/6147, 464XLAT RFC 6877, PREF64 RFC 8781, DHCP Option 108 RFC 8925); web-verified.

ipv6.title: Introduce IPv6 by phased dual-stack from a contained module, or carry it at the edge over the existing core (6PE/6VPE)
ipv6.recommended_action: Run dual-stack as the target transition state from a contained module after a HW/SW/app assessment + pilot; deliver IPv6 L3VPN with 6VPE (and 6PE for global) over the existing IPv4/MPLS core with per-PE rollout; provide RA-based IPv6 first-hop redundancy; reserve tunneling/NAT64 for transit/island cases.
ipv6.citation: CCDE Session 15 (dual-stack phased, RA HA); CCDE scenarios (6PE/6VPE over IPv4 core, avoid big-bang)

management.title: Enforce secure management (SSH/SNMPv3), centralized RBAC/AAA least-privilege, and retire plaintext
management.recommended_action: Standardize SNMPv3 + SSH, disable Telnet/SNMPv1-v2c, scope SNMP views; centralize AAA (TACACS+ command-authz/accounting + RADIUS access) with RBAC/least-privilege, guarded local fallback, banners and timeouts.
management.citation: CCDE Session 19 (secure management plane, SNMP versions, RBAC/AAA/least-privilege); engine CIS axis

management.title: Identify which CoPP class is dropping and why before the cutover — the policer is shielding the supervisor, not failing
management.recommended_action: Attribute, then decide — never blindly raise rates. (1) Pin down which class and how hard: on NX-OS `show policy-map interface control-plane` exposes per-class conformed vs. violated/dropped bytes plus the 5-minute violate rate and violated-peak timestamp; correlate the spike with a change/event window. (2) Classify the drop: map the class back to its CoPP ACL and confirm whether the source is legitimate control traffic at volume or anomalous (a single talker, a scan, a loop/glean storm — for glean specifically, fix next-hop reachability and enable `hardware ip glean throttle` rather than widening the policer). (3) If the traffic is legitimate and the rate is simply too small for this fleet, tune that specific class's CIR/BC upward from the appropriate default profile (strict/moderate/lenient/dense) — Cisco's guidance is to start from the default 'strict' policy and then customize per the protocols and scale actually present, treating CoPP as an ongoing baseline that must be revisited whenever devices/services are added (i.e. at every migration). (4) Re-measure to confirm drops for that class fall to zero/transient under normal load before declaring the control plane clean for the gate.
management.citation: Cisco 'Verify Control Plane Policing Violations on Nexus Platforms' (Doc ID 217946) — `show policy-map interface control-plane` violated/dropped-bytes and 5-min violate-rate interpretation, and triage of drops as attack vs. misconfiguration; with Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS Security Configuration Guide (Configure CoPP) — default 'strict' start point and per-class CIR/BC tuning as an ongoing process; and the Cisco 'Control Plane Policing Implementation Best Practices' note.

management.title: Wrap change in a reviewed lifecycle with rollback, version-control + drift detection, and templated/agentless automation
management.recommended_action: Introduce version control (Git) for config history/rollback and drift detection against a known-good baseline (+ software-image/inventory management); adopt a formal reviewed change lifecycle with mandatory rollback; deploy model-based templated/agentless automation with automated pre/post validation; run proactive threshold-based monitoring under an FCAPS/ITIL framework.
management.citation: CCDE Session 19 (change management, FCAPS configuration/drift, proactive monitoring); CCDE scenario (Git/Ansible/pyATS)

management.title: Build a dedicated out-of-band management network so management survives a data-plane outage
management.recommended_action: Stand up an OOB management network (terminal/console servers, dedicated mgmt interfaces or a separate mgmt VRF/VPN) reaching every critical device; keep in-band primary and OOB the always-available backup.
management.citation: CCDE Session 19 (in-band vs OOB, securing management plane)

management.title: Synchronize time (hierarchical NTP), centralize severity-tuned logging, and keep a current baseline + documentation
management.recommended_action: Deploy hierarchical authenticated NTP from trusted strata to the whole fleet; forward all logs to a central NTP-stamped syslog/SIEM with per-platform severity tuned to capture warnings/errors while suppressing chatty debug; capture and maintain a baseline + layered documentation via automated discovery.
management.citation: CCDE Session 19 (NTP stratum, syslog levels, baseline & documentation); engine CIS axis + baseline output

management.title: Build the OOB management network on physically separate gear so it survives a fabric meltdown and never transits the fabric it manages
management.recommended_action: Provision the OOB management network on dedicated, low-cost management switches separate from the production fabric, cabled to the devices' dedicated management ports (mgmt0 + ND/CIMC), and keep it off the user and storage data planes and off the VXLAN fabric; uplink to a redundant vPC OOB-aggregation pair with L3 to the A/S firewalls; never source the management path from the production ToR/FEX you may need to recover; size it for management traffic only (FE/GE), and use in-band (Loopback/VRF-management) only where a tool genuinely requires it. Treat reachability-during-a-meltdown -- not steady-state convenience -- as the design requirement.
management.citation: ipSpace.net DC Design Case Studies ch.6 'Designing a Private Cloud Network Infrastructure' (Management Network) (Pepelnjak); AJ SDD 'Fabric Management' / 'Out-of-Band Management'; Cisco DC management/OOB best practice

management.title: Move from polled SNMP toward NETCONF/YANG + streaming telemetry, and add active SLA measurement (IP SLA) and edge flow telemetry
management.recommended_action: Introduce NETCONF/YANG for transactional config and streaming telemetry for state (retain SNMPv3 only as fallback); deploy IP SLA probes per class on critical paths; enable IPFIX/NetFlow at the edge/peering on ingress, unsampled where blind spots are unacceptable.
management.citation: CCDE Session 19 / Session 17 (NETCONF/YANG RFC 3535, telemetry, IP SLA, NetFlow placement); CCDE scenario (IPFIX over vendor-specific)

methodology.title: Resolve duplicate-IP / overlapping-subnet collisions before merging any L3 domain
methodology.recommended_action: Build a target addressing plan that assigns globally-unique, summarisable space per zone; renumber the duplicates on the least-disruptive side ahead of the window; where a renumber is genuinely infeasible, document a NAT/NPTv6 bridge as a tracked exception with an owner and a removal plan. Re-run the conflict check until dup_ip / dup_subnet are zero before cutover.
methodology.citation: RFC 1918 (private address space); Cisco enterprise network-merger / migration addressing guidance (overlapping space -> renumber, or NAT/NPTv6 as an explicit exception).

methodology.title: Provide first-hop (gateway) redundancy on every L2-access default gateway
methodology.recommended_action: Introduce FHRP (HSRP or VRRP) on the distribution pair for every access VLAN gateway, or — where the platform supports it — eliminate FHRP via SVL/vPC single logical gateway or VXLAN-EVPN anycast gateway. Use VRRP for multivendor; keep GLBP off stateful Internet/firewall edges.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.1 (FHRP & L2 access); Cisco Campus CVD 2024 (SVL/anycast preferred over GLBP, VRRPv3 multivendor)

methodology.title: Treat unobserved FHRP/redundancy as UNKNOWN, never silently as healthy
methodology.recommended_action: Render 'FHRP absent' and 'not collected -> redundancy UNKNOWN' explicitly; never let a missing observation become a positive health claim. For the AJ DS/CS core + EVS vPC pair (uncollected), mark redundancy UNKNOWN and recommend collection.
methodology.citation: Repo doctrine (evidence-grounded, coverage-honest); commits ee3a362/642ee31 (FHRP false-health fix); analyze.py:1886 canonical FHRP gate

methodology.title: Drive EoL/EoS hardware out of critical roles and protect against the upgrade flag-day
methodology.recommended_action: Prioritize refresh of EoL/EoS devices in core/critical roles; specify dual-supervisor/dual-RP (SSO/NSF) or paired-node scale-out so upgrades/swaps are non-disruptive; sequence the migration so no single change becomes a flag-day.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Scalability (scale-out avoids the Flag Day) & Cost/TCO; engine EoL/software_risk axes

methodology.title: Right-size availability to the application and place in the network, not 5x9 everywhere
methodology.recommended_action: Classify sites/modules by criticality and assign an availability target per class; invest redundancy where MTBF/MTTR and app sensitivity justify it, and explicitly accept lower availability where the business does not require it.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 High Availability ('not every network needs 5x9/6x9'); CCDE Designer Skills (availability=MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR))

methodology.title: Detect failures with L1/BFD, not aggressively-tuned routing-protocol hellos
methodology.recommended_action: Enable BFD for IGP/BGP/static next-hops on links lacking a fast L1-down signal and leave hello/dead timers at default; prefer native L1 loss-of-signal/carrier-delay where the media provides it; reserve aggressive timers for last resort.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Convergence ('don't tune IGP hellos aggressively, use BFD'); CCDE OSPF/IS-IS BFD

methodology.title: Keep the core simple and fast; push intelligence, policy and stateful services to the edge
methodology.recommended_action: Relocate user termination, policy and stateful services to distribution/edge; reduce the core to a lean high-speed forwarding layer; on a collapsed core, plan separation of aggregation/services from forwarding as scale grows.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Network Topologies ('intelligence at the edge, core as simple as possible')

methodology.title: Resolve high-severity false-health masks (temporary bridges, masked faults) before baselining the design
methodology.recommended_action: For each high-severity false-health condition, determine what it is hiding (why the temporary bridge exists -- a failed uplink? a missing vPC peer-link? -- and what the masked fault is), remediate or remove the workaround, and re-collect so the current-state baseline reflects reality. Only then freeze the baseline, design the target from it, and take the NRFU pre-cutover snapshot. Track any condition that genuinely cannot be cleared pre-cutover as an explicit risk with an owner.
methodology.citation: Cisco NX-OS operational-health guidance (a 'show'-level healthy state can mask a real gap); Cisco Advanced Services pre-cutover baseline discipline (design from verified current state).

methodology.title: Minimize accidental complexity: every feature is one you must operate
methodology.recommended_action: Trace every protocol/feature/platform to a requirement; remove or avoid those without one. Consolidate on the fewest platforms that meet the needs; keep the core a simple, fast transport and concentrate policy/intelligence at the edge.
methodology.citation: ipSpace.net (Pepelnjak) 'Complexity Belongs to the Network Edge' / 'The Road to Complex Designs Is Paved with Great Recipes'

methodology.title: Pair every change step with a defined, TESTED rollback that restores the exact prior state, then verify the rollback
methodology.recommended_action: For every change block, author the exact reverse commands, dry-run them, and add explicit post-rollback verification that the device matches its captured pre-change baseline; keep each step independently reversible and capture the pre-change state before touching the device.
methodology.citation: EXPO2020 PSN Infra Hardening MOP §5 Rollback plan (§5.1 Undo the changes / §5.1.1 Post-Rollback checks); aligns with Cisco change-management leading practice. Distinct from mgmt-change-config-mgmt-automation.

methodology.title: Design in modular, replicable blocks with small fault domains
methodology.recommended_action: Restructure into hierarchical repeatable modules with summarization at each module edge; standardize per-module config so new blocks replicate quickly; keep a small site collapsed where modular separation is not cost-justified.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Modularity & M&A; CCDE Designer Skills (Modularity/Resiliency)

methodology.title: Summarize at the aggregation boundary to protect the core, accepting bounded sub-optimality
methodology.recommended_action: Configure summarization at the aggregation layer toward the core with contiguous per-module addressing; pair summaries with a discard/null route and component-aware advertisement to prevent black-holing of failed specifics.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Optimal Routing; Cisco Campus CVD (summarize at distribution)

methodology.title: Remediate physical-layer faults (CRC / input-errors / half-duplex / err-disable) before cutover
methodology.recommended_action: Triage and clear the physical faults before the window: reseat/replace optics and cabling on CRC/input-error ports, hard-set or correct duplex/speed on half-duplex links (no auto/half mismatch), and resolve the root cause behind each err-disable (don't just recover the port). Then re-baseline error counters to zero so NRFU can certify the cutover against a clean L1.
methodology.citation: IEEE 802.3 auto-negotiation (duplex mismatch -> late collisions / CRC); Cisco IOS/NX-OS interface error-counter troubleshooting; NRFU/ATP clean-baseline practice.

methodology.title: Classify every requirement (business / functional / application / technical / constraint) and trace decision-to-requirement
methodology.recommended_action: Run a requirements pass that records business goals, the application matrix (per-app latency/loss/bandwidth + flows), technical -ilities (availability/scale/security/manageability), and fixed constraints; structure as linked records so each design element maps to a requirement and a validation test.
methodology.citation: CCDE Study Guide Ch.1 (requirements taxonomy + constraints); Jama/ReqView RTM (forward/backward traceability); Orhan Ergun functional vs non-functional

methodology.title: Co-locate the STP root with the FHRP active gateway and enable preemption with delay
methodology.recommended_action: Align STP root priority and FHRP active (and stateful contexts) onto the same distribution node per VLAN; enable FHRP preempt with preempt-delay greater than measured switch boot/convergence time.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.1 (STP-FHRP interaction); CCDE Switching/DC ('HSRP active follow STP root', 'HSRP wait till STP converged')

methodology.title: Build redundancy as triangles, not squares or rings
methodology.recommended_action: Re-cable to triangle/partial-mesh between distribution and core so each node has a direct alternate path; dual-home every access switch and bond uplinks (vPC/VSS/MLAG) so both forward.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Network Topologies ('Build Triangles, Not Squares'); CCDE Switching/DC Q1

methodology.title: Score every decision against the canonical trade-off axes and name one ranked primary driver
methodology.recommended_action: For each consequential decision emit {decision, driving_requirement, primary_axis, axis_scores, tensions_accepted, constraint_bounds}; require the primary driver to be explicit so the trade-off is auditable.
methodology.citation: Oppenheimer Top-Down Network Design (8 canonical axes, fixed-budget framing); CCDE In Depth Ch.2 (design = managing trade-offs)

methodology.title: Design top-down from business and application requirements (know the WHY)
methodology.recommended_action: Before recommending target-state changes, gather and record the requirement set (business goals, critical apps + delay/jitter/loss/availability needs, growth, constraints/budget) and justify each design decision by tracing it to a specific requirement; prefer the simplest solution that meets it.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth (Ergun) Ch.2 'Know the purpose of your design'; Oppenheimer Top-Down Network Design (requirements-first); CCDE WHY->WHAT->HOW

methodology.title: Size each switch's replacement for its load plus a growth headroom -- don't port a near-full switch 1:1
methodology.recommended_action: Size the target from observed port_util/poe_util plus a documented growth headroom (e.g. +30-50%) AND the build-before-break overhead; prefer higher-density or modular platforms where switches are saturated; verify the PoE budget covers the powered-endpoint load with margin. Carry the headroom assumption into the BoM, not just the slide.
methodology.citation: Cisco Enterprise Campus / CVD capacity & oversubscription planning (size for growth, not 1:1); IEEE 802.3af/at/bt PoE power budgeting.

methodology.title: Avoid redistribution where possible; where unavoidable, fence it with route tags and filters
methodology.recommended_action: Where feasible converge onto one common IGP and delete redistribution; where it must stay, make it one-way if possible, redistribute at multiple points for redundancy, and tag-and-filter (deny the tag on re-entry) at every mutual point.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Load Balancing/Redistribution & M&A; CCDE EIGRP/IGP-comparison

methodology.title: Use only necessary redundancy — two is company, three is a crowd
methodology.recommended_action: Standardize on dual redundancy for critical paths/nodes and remove the third+ tier; prefer the configuration that meets the requirement with the fewest steps; collapse overlapping HA features to one mechanism per failure mode.
methodology.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 Simplicity ('two's company, three's a crowd'; too much redundancy increases MTTR)

mpls-te.title: Choose the protection layer (L1 / IGP+BFD / MPLS-TE FRR) and FRR scope (link vs node) by failure model
mpls-te.recommended_action: Map each protected service to the cheapest layer meeting its target (FRR ~50ms for hard real-time, tuned IGP+BFD for general, L1 only where transport provides it); use link-FRR by default, node-FRR for real P-node risk, and SRLG-disjoint primary/backup.
mpls-te.citation: CCDE Session 9 (protection L1/L2/L3, FRR link/node, SRLG); CCDE scenario (SRLG same-duct, TI-LFA diverse paths)

mpls-te.title: Enable LDP-IGP synchronization and loopback label hygiene to prevent black-holing
mpls-te.recommended_action: Enable LDP-IGP synchronization + session protection across the core; loopback-source sessions/router-IDs and filter label allocation to loopback /32s; run MPLS OAM (LSP ping/traceroute, LSP-BFD) on tunnels and pseudowires.
mpls-te.citation: CCDE Session 7 (LDP-IGP sync, loopback label hygiene, MPLS OAM)

mpls-te.title: Enable IGP TE extensions to feed CSPF and confine TE state to the core
mpls-te.recommended_action: Turn on IGP TE extensions across the TE domain and advertise reservable bandwidth/TE-metric/affinity per link; scope TE to core PoP-to-PoP routers with RSVP auto-mesh, keeping access on LDP/IGP.
mpls-te.citation: CCDE Session 9 (IGP TE extensions, core-only scope, auto-mesh)

mpls-te.title: Deploy MPLS-TE only for a concrete driver, and use RSVP-TE (not LDP) for constraint-based LSPs
mpls-te.recommended_action: State the driver first; deploy RSVP-TE with CSPF for the constrained flows (keep LDP for any-to-any), tactical tunnels for hot spots then a strategic mesh, and consider SR-TE to drop per-LSP state.
mpls-te.citation: CCDE Session 9 (TE drivers, LDP cannot build CBR LSPs); CCDE scenario (tactical->strategic TE)

multicast.title: Make the RP redundant (Anycast-RP + MSDP for SM; Phantom-RP for Bidir) and place it near sources
multicast.recommended_action: Deploy Anycast-RP (shared loopback on 2+ routers) + MSDP for SM/Bidir-source sharing; use Phantom-RP for Bidir; locate the RP near source aggregation.

multicast.title: Treat multicast as a security surface and enable IGMP snooping + group limits at the L2 edge
multicast.recommended_action: Scope 239/8 with boundaries (and Auto-RP/BSR filters), remove PIM from untrusted edges, enable IGMP/MLD snooping with a querier per active VLAN, set per-port group limits, and adopt a clean group-address plan.
multicast.citation: CCDE Session 11/12 (multicast boundary, no edge PIM, IGMP snooping/limits, addressing); engine build_igmp_queriers + vlan_inventory

multicast.title: Give a broadcast (ST 2110) media fabric a resilient PTP timing plane: SMPTE ST 2059-2, boundary clocks, redundant grandmasters
multicast.recommended_action: Deploy >=2 GNSS-locked grandmasters (redundant, ST 2059-2 profile); enable boundary clock on every media-path switch; place the media plane in a dedicated VRF/zone with IGMPv3/SSM; verify all clocks lock and converge inside the ~1 microsecond accuracy budget.
multicast.citation: SMPTE ST 2059-2 (PTP broadcast profile) + ST 2110-10 timing; boundary-clock + redundant-grandmaster leading practice (The Broadcast Bridge / KeyCode Media / Leader-Phabrix); web-verified.

multicast.title: Keep a reachable rendezvous point (RP) for every running PIM sparse-mode domain (or move groups to SSM)
multicast.recommended_action: Restore RP reachability/election (static RP with anycast-RP redundancy, Auto-RP, or BSR), verify each running PIM device learns the RP, or migrate the affected groups to SSM; re-verify before the cutover baseline.
multicast.citation: RFC 7761 (PIM-SM); Cisco PIM RP configuration & verification (Auto-RP / BSR / static / anycast-RP); web-verified.

multicast.title: Resolve any (S,G) with a Null RPF incoming interface (a blackholed multicast source-tree)
multicast.recommended_action: Verify the unicast route and RPF neighbour toward the source ('show ip rpf <source>'); fix the missing / incorrect route, the broken PIM adjacency on the upstream path, or the static-mroute / RPF-override that should bridge a unicast/multicast topology divergence; re-verify the (S,G) IIF is non-Null before the multicast path is on the cutover plan.
multicast.citation: Cisco IP Multicast / PIM design guides (the RPF check and 'show ip rpf'); RFC 7761 (PIM-SM) RPF forwarding rule; the RPF-failure / Null-IIF outage class

multicast.title: Default to PIM Sparse-Mode (explicit-join); never run Dense-Mode, and prevent dense fallback
multicast.recommended_action: Standardize on PIM Sparse-Mode, define an explicit (redundant) RP, remove dense-mode from data interfaces, and use the Auto-RP listener instead of sparse-dense; migrate legacy dense-mode to sparse.
multicast.citation: CCDE Session 11 (PIM modes, autorp-listener); CCDE scenario (migrate dense->sparse); engine build_igmp_queriers

multicast.title: Select SSM / ASM / Bidir from the source-receiver pattern and the state-vs-optimality trade-off
multicast.recommended_action: Use SSM (232/8 + IGMPv3) for one-to-many with known sources; ASM where sources are unknown; Bidir for many-to-many; set SPT-threshold 0 for latency-sensitive SM; extend state lifetime or use Bidir/SSM for bursty sources.
multicast.citation: CCDE Session 11/12 (SSM/ASM/Bidir, SPT-threshold, intermittent sources); CCDE scenarios (mode by pattern)

multicast.title: Repair RPF failures over tunnels/asymmetry, and bridge multicast across incapable transit (MSDP+MBGP, AMT, overlay)
multicast.recommended_action: Add a static mroute toward the tunnel/correct upstream (verifying register/join paths) or run MBGP; peer RPs with MSDP + MBGP across domains; use AMT or a customer overlay to carry multicast/IPv6 over incapable transit — never downgrade multicast to unicast.
multicast.citation: CCDE Session 12 (RPF/mroute, MSDP/MBGP, AMT); CCDE scenarios (overlay over incapable SP)

multicast.title: Never assume a missing IGMP querier fails open: snooping-without-querier floods on some platforms and black-holes on others -- guarantee a querier
multicast.recommended_action: Require a confirmed IGMP querier on every active multicast VLAN (a router by default, else the designated lowest-IP snooping switch); do not depend on the snooping-flood fallback as a safety net; in mixed fleets explicitly verify the no-querier behaviour of the receiver-hosting platforms before cutover.
multicast.citation: Cisco IGMP-snooping case study (no-mrouter/querier behaviour differs across Catalyst families -- some flood, some prune); web-verified that no-querier snooping behaviour is implementation-specific, not standardised.

observability.title: Alert on multi-window, multi-burn-rate error-budget consumption, not on raw threshold crossings
observability.recommended_action: Design the observability alerting as a small set of burn-rate tiers, each with two windows (short approximately one-twelfth of the long), tied to the service's SLO: a high-burn-rate pair that pages, and a low-burn-rate pair that opens a ticket. Tune burn-rate multiples and windows to the SLO target and acceptable alert volume, and make resetting/recovery explicit. Avoid raw per-counter threshold alarms as the primary reliability signal.
observability.citation: Google The Site Reliability Workbook, 'Alerting on SLOs' (multiwindow, multi-burn-rate alerting), sre.google/workbook

observability.title: Define reliability as SLI/SLO/error-budget contracts, not 'five-nines everywhere'
observability.recommended_action: For the target-state design, attach an SLI definition (the exact good/total ratio and window) and an SLO target to each critical service tier, and write an error-budget policy that states what happens to change-freeze and release cadence as the budget depletes. Differentiate targets by tier rather than applying one number fleet-wide. Capture these as named requirements so the deliverables carry the reliability contract, not just the topology.
observability.citation: Google SRE Book, 'Service Level Objectives'; The Site Reliability Workbook, 'Implementing SLOs' (sre.google)

operations.title: Discover and inventory undocumented (shadow) infrastructure before baselining the design
operations.recommended_action: Identify each shadow node from the advertising device+port and its CDP/LLDP platform/mgmt IP, then add it to the inventory and collect it (or formally scope it out WITH the customer and record it). Re-run discovery until every infra neighbour reconciles, then freeze the baseline.
operations.citation: Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP) + IEEE 802.1AB LLDP capability codes (Switch/Router vs Trans-Bridge/Host/Phone); Cisco PPDIOO Prepare/Plan network-discovery & inventory-completeness practice.

optical-transport.title: Choose the ROADM add/drop architecture by the flexibility tier actually needed (colorless / directionless / contentionless), not maximal CDC by default
optical-transport.recommended_action: When an optical/DWDM transport layer is in scope, state the target add/drop tier per ROADM site (fixed mux/demux vs colorless, +directionless, +contentionless, +flex-grid) and justify it from the wavelength-churn and remote-reconfiguration requirement; size contentionless nodes so drop units match the degree count. This engine collects no photonic state, so it cannot detect the installed ROADM tier -- carry this as a design-questionnaire item and an HLD optical-layer decision, never inferred from the assessed L1-L4 evidence.
optical-transport.citation: Cisco ONS 15454 & NCS 2000 DWDM Network Configuration Guides (colorless/directionless/contentionless ROADM, flex-spectrum SMR line cards); Cisco Transport Planner

optical-transport.title: Decide the IP-over-DWDM layer-collapse (Routed Optical Networking) vs a transponder-based optical layer as an explicit architecture trade -- faceplate power/OSNR and open-line-system ownership are the constraints
optical-transport.recommended_action: When optical transport is in scope, state whether the target is IPoDWDM/Routed-Optical-Networking (coherent pluggables in the router over an open line system) or a transponder-based optical layer, and justify it against per-span reach/OSNR feasibility, the 400ZR-vs-OpenZR+ profile, and who owns the open-line-system fault domain. The engine sees no optical reach/OSNR/line-system data, so this stays an HLD decision and design-interview item; do not infer optical feasibility from the L1-L4 assessment.
optical-transport.citation: Cisco Routed Optical Networking design guidance; OIF 400ZR Implementation Agreement and OpenZR+ MSA white paper

optical-transport.title: Engineer the IPoDWDM optical link as a first-class budget (Tx power / OSNR / add-drop) and operate IP and optical as one cross-layer fault domain
optical-transport.recommended_action: For every coherent IPoDWDM link, produce and verify an optical link budget (grid channel, Tx power vs line-system add/drop, span loss, Rx OSNR margin) at design time, and stand up cross-layer fault correlation (unified IP+optical inventory and assurance, OpenConfig/IETF/ACTN-aligned) so optical degradations are correlated to root cause rather than misdiagnosed as IP instability; gate the link's NRFU on a Tx/Rx power-continuity validation through the optical add/drop.
optical-transport.citation: IETF ACTN framework (RFC 8453); OIF 400ZR Implementation Agreement (Rx OSNR); Cisco Routed Optical Networking Solution Guide cross-layer fault correlation

optical-transport.title: Plan optical-layer survivability as a deliberate choice between hard wavelength protection and GMPLS/WSON dynamic restoration -- colorless+tunable add/drop is the enabler, contention is the failure mode
optical-transport.recommended_action: For any DWDM/OTN transport in scope, decide per service class whether it gets dedicated optical protection or GMPLS/WSON restoration, and validate that restorable circuits have a spectrum/wavelength-feasible alternate path (no contention) under the single-failure cases. This is HLD optical-survivability doctrine: the engine collects no Layer-0 control-plane or wavelength state, so it cannot compute optical restorability -- never let absence of optical evidence read as 'optical layer is protected'.
optical-transport.citation: ITU-T/GMPLS WSON optical control-plane principles as applied in Cisco WSON / NCS optical control-plane design; Fibre Systems 'The case for SDN-based optical network restoration'

optical-transport.title: Plan router host-port power, thermal headroom and faceplate density for coherent pluggables, and unify IP+optical fault/PM under one telemetry plane
optical-transport.recommended_action: Validate per-port power/thermal and supported-slot rules before populating coherent optics (don't assume every 400G port takes a ZR+ at full reach); and stand up a single IP+optical telemetry/alarm model (streaming optical PM + coherent alarms with IP-to-line-system fault correlation) instead of a separate optical EMS.
optical-transport.citation: Cisco Routed Optical Networking Solution Guide Rel 4.0 / Routed Optical Networking HLD (xrdocs.io) -- ZR/ZR+ power classes, host placement, model-driven management; OpenZR+ MSA white paper (15W vs 25W module power targets)
