optical-transport.title: Prefer IP-over-DWDM (faceplate coherent ZR/ZR+ pluggables) over a separate transponder layer when the router supports it -- collapse the optical layer, but engineer the line system and OSNR budget
optical-transport.recommended_action: For new DCI/metro links, default to faceplate coherent pluggables (IPoDWDM) where the platform and reach allow; require an explicit optical link-budget worksheet (per-channel launch power, span loss, amplifier/ROADM insertion loss, margin, receive OSNR vs the optic's threshold) and an alien-wavelength interop sign-off with the line-system vendor before committing the design.
optical-transport.citation: OIF 400ZR / OpenZR+ IA; ITU-T G.698.2 (amplified multichannel DWDM application code / alien wavelength) and G.680; Cisco Routed Optical Networking design guidance

optical-transport.title: Select the coherent pluggable (400ZR vs OpenZR+/ZR+) from the actual span reach and line-system type, not from the line rate alone
optical-transport.recommended_action: For each IPoDWDM link, choose the coherent pluggable from the span budget: 400ZR (fixed 16QAM/CFEC) for unamplified <=~40 km or amplified <=~120 km point-to-point; OpenZR+/ZR+ (oFEC, multi-rate/multi-modulation, ~25 W) for longer amplified spans, ROADM-traversing wavelengths, or where sub-rate multiplexing is needed -- and verify the router port supplies the module's power/cooling envelope.
optical-transport.citation: OIF 400ZR Implementation Agreement; OpenZR+ MSA Technical Specification; Cisco 400G QSFP-DD Digital Coherent Optics Data Sheet (QDD-400G-ZR-S / QDD-400G-ZRP-S)

optical-transport.title: Select the DCI optical transport tier from fiber availability, reach and capacity: grey optics, then pluggable DWDM (ZR/ZR+), then transponder DWDM
optical-transport.recommended_action: When a design spans buildings/sites over owned or leased fiber, state the optical tier explicitly with its justification: grey if fiber is abundant and reach is short; pluggable DWDM (ZR/ZR+) if fiber is constrained or capacity is high; transponder DWDM only for long-haul or extreme channel density. Record which axis (fiber scarcity vs reach vs capacity vs cost) was the ranked primary driver.
optical-transport.citation: OIF 400ZR Implementation Agreement; OpenZR+ MSA white paper (rev 0.92, 2023); Cisco 'Routed Optical Networking / Coherent Pluggable Optics' Solution Overview

optical-transport.title: Split survivability across layers on a DWDM core: optical-layer 1+1/1+1+R (with SRLG-diverse fibers) for wavelength services, IP-layer TI-LFA/FRR for packet services -- and never double-protect the same failure twice
optical-transport.recommended_action: On any DWDM/IPoDWDM core, document a multilayer survivability matrix: which failure classes are recovered at the optical layer (and the scheme: 1+1 / 1:1 / 1+1+R) vs the IP layer (TI-LFA/FRR), enforce SRLG/conduit diversity on the working+protect fibers, and explicitly forbid protecting the same failure at both layers. Tie hold-off timers so the faster layer acts first.
optical-transport.citation: ITU-T G.808/G.873 (optical protection architectures 1+1/1:1); RFC 9855 (Segment-Routing TI-LFA, SRLG-aware sub-50ms IP FRR)

qos.title: Prefer DiffServ (class-based PHB) over per-flow IntServ/RSVP at scale, and don't run both as the QoS model
qos.recommended_action: Adopt a DiffServ class-of-service model (mark at the edge, enforce CS/AF/EF PHBs hop-by-hop); reserve RSVP for MPLS-TE/CAC niches only.
qos.citation: CCDE Session 10 (IntServ limits vs DiffServ); CCDE scenario (don't mix IntServ+DiffServ)

qos.title: Characterize egress queue drops and prove they spare sensitive classes before freezing the QoS baseline
qos.recommended_action: Diagnose by isolating the queue, not by globally widening buffers. (1) Confirm and rate the drops with 'show interfaces <intf>' (total output drops and trend) — a tiny, stable count on a best-effort class may be acceptable; a growing count or any count on a priority class is not. (2) On Catalyst 9000, attribute drops to a specific queue with 'show platform hardware fed switch active qos queue stats interface <intf>' and inspect the buffer allocation with 'show platform hardware fed switch active qos queue config interface <intf>' (Hardmax/Softmax); on routers/MQC platforms use 'show policy-map interface <intf>' to see per-class queue and drop counters. (3) Determine the cause class — sustained oversubscription (a capacity/topology fix), microbursts (a buffer/queue-limit fix), or a queueing policy that starves a class. (4) For microbursts, raise the shared-buffer headroom first as the low-risk mitigation ('qos queue-softmax-multiplier', default 100, up to the platform maximum) and/or tune the specific queue-limit; for a class being starved, correct the egress queuing/bandwidth policy so priority traffic is protected. (5) For genuine oversubscription, the real fix is capacity (more/faster uplinks, load-balancing, or moving the talker) — buffers only defer the loss. Re-verify per-queue stats after the change and confirm sensitive classes show zero drops.
qos.citation: Cisco — Troubleshoot Output Drops on Catalyst 9000 Switches (per-queue 'show platform hardware fed ... qos queue stats/config', Hardmax/Softmax buffers, microburst mitigation via qos queue-softmax-multiplier)

qos.title: Establish a QoS trust boundary at the edge and a coherent end-to-end policy from app requirements
qos.recommended_action: Define a trust boundary at the access edge (trust phones/markings, re-mark untrusted ports), deploy a consistent end-to-end queuing policy sized to the app budgets, and unify divergent per-site QoS into one standard; trust access markings in the core rather than re-classifying.
qos.citation: CCDE In Depth Ch.2 M&A & Applications (150ms/30ms/1%); engine compute_qos_audit; Cisco Borderless Campus QoS

qos.title: Give voice strict priority but bound it; separate TCP/UDP and real-time subclasses; WRED for TCP only
qos.recommended_action: Place voice in a bounded LLQ/EF class with a policer; give signaling and each video type its own class; separate TCP from UDP; apply (W)RED to TCP/AF classes only and exempt voice/UDP.
qos.citation: CCDE Session 10 (LLQ bounding, TCP/UDP separation, WRED for TCP); CCDE scenario (RFC4594, WRED TCP-only)

qos.title: Derive a lean DSCP/PHB class model from the application profile and align it to platform/WAN limits
qos.recommended_action: Define and roll out an RFC-4594 DSCP/PHB scheme at the edge; consolidate to the lean class set the platform and WAN both support; mark close to source and trust those marks downstream.
qos.citation: CCDE Session 10 (RFC 4594, minimize classes, close-to-source); CCDE scenario (1 PQ + N BQ from app matrix)

qos.title: Shape egress to the contracted rate before the SP polices, and queue at every congestion point
qos.recommended_action: Apply hierarchical egress shaping on the CE to the CIR with a child queuing policy; deploy egress queuing at each congestion point (access uplinks, distribution/core aggregation, WAN edge); over-provision and keep coarse classes on an owned core, or skip core QoS where it is genuinely uncongested.
qos.citation: CCDE Session 10 (shape-before-police, queue everywhere, core over-provision); CCDE scenario (no QoS on owned uncongested core)

routing.title: Restore the down BFD session before baselining — its protected protocol has lost sub-second failure detection
routing.recommended_action: Work the session from the bottom of the stack up. (1) Confirm the underlying L1/L2 path and IP reachability first — `show bfd neighbors [details]` for the session's last-down diagnostic, plus `show ip interface brief` / line-protocol on the interface; a flapping or down interface is the usual root cause. (2) If the link is up, rule out a configuration asymmetry: BFD must be enabled on BOTH peers, and the operating mode (asynchronous vs. echo) and the negotiated tx/rx/multiplier timers must be compatible — a one-sided 'bfd interval' or an echo-mode mismatch leaves the session stuck Down. (3) Confirm the protocol client is actually registered (e.g. `bfd` under the BGP neighbor / `bfd all-interfaces` under OSPF) — BFD with no client does nothing. (4) Verify nothing is dropping the BFD control packets on the path: an interface ACL that permits BFD but carries the `log` keyword, or that misses UDP/3784 (and the echo-source for multihop), will break the session even though data forwards; check CoPP on the supervisor for BFD-class drops too. (5) Only once the session reaches Up with stable timers do you re-baseline and treat fast-failover as available for the gate.
routing.citation: IETF RFC 5880, Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) — session states (Down/Init/Up) and diagnostic codes (Control Detection Time Expired / Echo Function Failed / Neighbor Signaled Session Down); BFD reports state change to registered clients which take action. Corroborated by Cisco 'Troubleshoot Bidirectional Forwarding Detection in Cisco IOS XE' (Doc ID 220364) — UDP/3784, async vs echo, ACL-log breakage, `show bfd neighbors details`.

routing.title: Make gateway failover deterministic: pair FHRP preempt with interface/object tracking before baselining
routing.recommended_action: Resolve per group, primary side first: (1) Decide intended roles — set explicit priorities (do not leave both peers at the 100 default) so primary > secondary, and document which device should own each VLAN's gateway. (2) Add tracking on the device whose uplink loss should trigger hand-off — prefer enhanced object tracking (track an object for line-protocol or IP-routing state, or an IP SLA/route reachability object) over the legacy 'standby track <if>' so a tracked-uplink failure decrements priority below the peer; size the decrement so the crossover actually occurs (decrement > priority gap). (3) Enable preempt on the higher-priority router so it both reclaims after recovery and so a tracking-driven decrement on its peer results in a real failover. (4) Add 'preempt delay minimum' (and 'standby delay minimum reload') so a recovering/rebooting router waits for its routing table and uplinks to converge before seizing the gateway, avoiding a transient black hole. (5) For dual-supervisor/stacked platforms keep SSO/HSRP-aware redundancy so a switchover doesn't bounce the role. (6) Re-collect and confirm tracking decrements and preempt are present and roles match design before freezing the baseline.
routing.citation: Cisco IOS XE First Hop Redundancy Protocols Configuration Guide — Configuring HSRP (standby preempt, standby track / object tracking, preempt delay); Cisco support doc 'Use Standby Preempt and Standby Track Commands'; RFC 2281 Cisco Hot Standby Router Protocol (priority/preemption/Coup, 3s/10s timers)

routing.title: Reconcile any broken FHRP group (no-active, dual-active/split, or split-brain) before freezing the cutover baseline
routing.recommended_action: Treat this as a fault to clear before any cutover-readiness sign-off, diagnosing toward the single invariant 'one Active, one Standby': (1) On both peers capture FHRP state and history (e.g. show standby / show standby brief, show standby <vlan>, plus the group's recent state transitions and any STANDBY-3-DUPADDR or 'received own hello' logs) to classify the state and find the last transition's trigger. (2) Verify the L2 path carrying the group VLAN between the peers is up end-to-end — the trunk/port-channel, the VLAN's allowed list, and STP forwarding for that VLAN; a down or pruned inter-switch link is the first suspect for a split. (3) Confirm the peers can actually exchange hellos: check that the HSRP transport (multicast 224.0.0.2 / UDP 1985, or IPv6 FF02::66) is not filtered by an ACL or dropped by CoPP, that the link is bidirectional, and that MTU is consistent. (4) Reconcile configuration symmetry — same group number, same HSRP version, matching authentication, and consistent timers on both peers. (5) Rule out resource exhaustion — CPU/interface drops starving the hellos. (6) Once a single Active is restored, set explicit priority + preempt + tracking so the recovered state is also deterministic, then re-collect and confirm one-Active/one-Standby before baselining.
routing.citation: Cisco support doc 'Troubleshoot HSRP Common Issues' (dual-active / duplicate-address / lost-hello causes and fixes) and 'Avoiding HSRP Instability in a Switching Environment'; RFC 2281 Cisco Hot Standby Router Protocol (single active router forwards; hello/hold 3s/10s; active-timer expiry → standby becomes active)

routing.title: Re-point or dynamic-ize static default routes before any gateway/next-hop change (cutover black-hole)
routing.recommended_action: Inventory every static-default host and its next-hop; for each, decide the target default path and SEQUENCE its update into the cutover step for that device (or pre-stage a floating/tracked static + a dynamic default so it fails over instead of black-holing). Prefer migrating edge defaults to a dynamic protocol (or object-tracked static with IP SLA) so a future gateway change reconverges on its own. Validate reachability to the off-subnet world in NRFU after each re-point.
routing.citation: Cisco routing design — a static default route does not reconverge; use a dynamic default, or an object-tracked / floating static (IP SLA) for gateway resilience; Cisco migration practice — re-point or dynamic-ize static next-hops before changing the gateway they point at.

scenario-pattern.title: Terminate overlays from untrusted/partner sites on a dedicated device behind the firewall, not on the core/Internet edge
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Land the overlay on a dedicated termination router behind the firewall so decapsulated traffic is statefully inspected before entering the internal network and a fault in the external sites cannot destabilize the core/edge.
scenario-pattern.citation: CCDE MilkaTurka scenario (GRE termination placement: failure isolation + stateful inspection)

scenario-pattern.title: Preserve dual-homed endpoints across move-groups -- move both attachment points together
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Constrain the move-group/wave generator so BOTH attachment switches of each dual-homed endpoint land in the SAME wave; validate per wave that each endpoint still has two live paths after the move; and classify every shared-IP set (legitimate FHRP/anycast vs a real duplicate to renumber) before cutover.
scenario-pattern.citation: Cisco Advanced Services migration move-group methodology (preserve endpoint redundancy across waves); NIC-teaming / dual-homing dependency on both network paths.

scenario-pattern.title: Gather the decision-driving requirements before designing — never assume, never re-ask what's given
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Before committing a design choice, confirm the specific decision-driving inputs (existing/partner equipment capability, data security level, convergence/SLA target, application matrix, provider coverage/feature support); design to stated requirements, not reflexive best practice, and never re-ask facts already given.
scenario-pattern.citation: CCDE MilkaTurka & Ornio scenarios (requirements-gathering, no-assumptions); CCDE Scenario 1/2 (SLA + app matrix + device utilization first)

scenario-pattern.title: Migrate through a transit/bridge site with build-before-break, parallel-running old and new until validated
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Choose a transit site; establish new circuits + routing at transit then remote; set metrics so new is preferred while old remains fallback; enable QoS + monitoring; remove old circuits remote-first/transit-last; keep every step reversible and validate with a pre/post snapshot diff.
scenario-pattern.citation: CCDE Ornio scenario (MPLS L3VPN migration step ordering); engine --compare/--trend snapshot diff

scenario-pattern.title: Size redundancy (second path, BFD, fast timers) to the application's actual convergence requirement, not reflexive best practice
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Provision a single path/default timers for loose convergence targets; reserve dual-homing/BFD/feasible-successor/aggressive timers for apps with tight recovery needs; record the convergence target as the design basis.
scenario-pattern.citation: CCDE MilkaTurka scenario (one-vs-two tunnels per store; BFD/feasible-successor under loose convergence)

scenario-pattern.title: At large branch scale optimize for OpEx (reuse existing edge via tunnels) over CapEx (new device+circuit per site)
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Default to an overlay tunnel over existing/partner edge and existing transport; add per-site hardware/circuits only where a hard requirement demands it, justified against multiplied OpEx.

scenario-pattern.title: Move the default gateway (SVI) LAST for any subnet whose endpoints straddle multiple switches
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: In each move-group, schedule the SVI/default-gateway move as the final step for every straddling subnet; keep the legacy gateway active and the target BD flooding (ARP/unknown-unicast) on with unicast routing off until all workloads are across; only then move the gateway and enable routing.
scenario-pattern.citation: Cisco 'Migrating Existing Networks to ACI' (BD flood on / unicast-routing off until workloads move; gateway last); web-verified.

scenario-pattern.title: Resolve merger address/AS-number collisions with NAT44 and BGP Local-AS, plan re-addressing as the clean fix
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Interconnect overlapping space with NAT44 (not PAT) for bidirectional auditable reachability; bridge duplicate ASNs with BGP Local-AS as an interim; schedule re-addressing/AS-redesign as the clean long-term fix.
scenario-pattern.citation: CCDE Scenario 1 (NAT44 vs PAT, Local-AS / AS redesign); Ornio (overlap blocks Option C)

scenario-pattern.title: Overlay a customer tunnel to deliver a service the provider/transport cannot carry (multicast, IPv6, encryption)
scenario-pattern.recommended_action: Build a customer GRE/DMVPN overlay (IPsec where confidentiality is needed) over the provider transport to carry the unsupported service end-to-end; reuse an existing resiliency overlay for multicast/IPv6 rather than downgrading to unicast.
scenario-pattern.citation: CCDE Ornio/ADF scenarios (overlay-over-L3VPN / GRE over dense-only SP)

sd-wan.title: Steer each application to a transport meeting its measured SLA class (loss/latency/jitter), and decide the no-path-meets-SLA behaviour per class
sd-wan.recommended_action: Define a lean set of SLA classes (max loss/latency/jitter), map apps to classes via DSCP/application classification, bind them in app-aware-routing policy; tune the BFD hello-interval for liveness and the app-route poll-interval/multiplier for SLA responsiveness separately; and explicitly choose strict (drop) vs loose/backup fallback per class and document it.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco SD-WAN Application-Aware Routing deploy guide + SD-WAN labs; web-verified (BFD probes, SLA classes, strict vs backup-sla).

sd-wan.title: Break out SaaS/Internet locally (DIA) instead of backhauling, and place branch security per site: on-box ZBFW/IPS/URL/AMP vs cloud SIG
sd-wan.recommended_action: Steer trusted SaaS/web/IaaS to local DIA, reserving backhaul only for traffic that must transit the core (regulated/legacy-central); choose security placement per site -- on-box ZBFW+IPS+URL+AMP where the branch is large, latency/compliance-sensitive, or must inspect during a cloud outage; cloud SIG where light branches favour a thin edge; commonly a hybrid (on-box as the SIG-down fallback).
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN security design (on-box stack vs Umbrella SIG; DIA) + SD-WAN labs; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Split policy by plane: centralized CONTROL policy moves routes/TLOCs/topology on the Controller; LOCALIZED data policy acts on packets at the edge
sd-wan.recommended_action: Author fabric-wide steering/segmentation/app-route as centralized control + data policy on the Controller (site-list/VPN-list scoped, directional); reserve localized policy for genuinely interface-scoped ACL/QoS; standardize edges on centralized device/feature templates with per-device divergence as keyed variables, and route all fleet change through template edits.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Policy + Templates design guidance + SD-WAN labs; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Restore the down WAN-edge control connection before freezing the SD-WAN cutover baseline
sd-wan.recommended_action: Work the controller's own verdict, outside-in: (1) read `show sdwan control connections-history` and pivot on the LOCAL/REMOTE ERROR mnemonic rather than guessing. (2) Prove underlay reachability and routing to each controller TLOC (ICMP/traceroute, valid RIB next-hop, correct color/public-private mapping, and firewall/NAT pinholes for 12346+/DTLS or the TLS port). (3) Verify time: confirm NTP is synchronized on the edge and controllers (a skewed clock invalidates certificates and breaks the handshake). (4) Validate identity: certificate validity and the enterprise root-CA installed on the edge (`show sdwan certificate root-ca-cert`), the organization-name match, and that the device UUID/serial is authorized — then re-push the WAN-edge list with Configuration > Certificates > Send to Controllers. (5) Re-check that all expected connections (vBond/vManage/vSmart, both transports) are UP and stable, not flapping. Resolve to green and re-snapshot before the cutover gate.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco — Troubleshoot SD-WAN Control Connections (Doc ID 214509; control connections-history error codes DCONFAIL/CRTVERFL/CTORGNMMIS/SERNTPRES/BIDNTVRFD, DTLS/TLS, certificate + root-CA + WAN-edge-list checks)

sd-wan.title: Re-establish the unreachable device's controller reporting before treating its state as known-good
sd-wan.recommended_action: (1) Read the connection history and identify which peer timed out (VB_TMO/VM_TMO/VP_TMO/VS_TMO) — that names the lost relationship. (2) Establish underlay reachability to the controllers (ICMP/traceroute) and confirm a valid RIB route with the correct next-hop/TLOC; control connections never form over a broken underlay. (3) Check time first — verify NTP/clock sync on the device and controllers, since skew makes a good certificate look expired and silently breaks the handshake. (4) Validate identity: certificate validity, enterprise root-CA present on the device, organization-name match, and the device serial/UUID in the WAN-edge list — then Configuration > Certificates > WAN Edge List > Send to Controllers to re-sync. (5) If reachability/identity are clean but the device is still not reporting, look vManage-side (NMS/DPI load, cluster/disk health). (6) Confirm the device is back to a full, stable control state and re-collect its evidence so the baseline reflects observed — not assumed — state.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco — Troubleshoot Connection When Devices Lose Connectivity to vManage (Doc ID 218077; peer-timeout codes VB_TMO/VM_TMO/VP_TMO/VS_TMO, reachability + RIB/TLOC, certificate 'Send to Controllers', NTP/clock sync)

sd-wan.title: Segment the WAN end-to-end with service VPNs carried in one tunnel; reserve VPN 0 for transport and VPN 512 for OOB management
sd-wan.recommended_action: Map each isolation domain to one service VPN before build; keep all WAN/TLOC interfaces in transport VPN 0 and device management in VPN 512; map each LAN segment into exactly one service VPN; make all inter-VPN reachability explicit (route-leak or service insertion), never implicit.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN segmentation design (service VPNs, VPN 0 / VPN 512) + SD-WAN labs; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Adopt SD-WAN as a four-plane controller fabric (Manager/Controller/Validator/WAN-Edge); only the data plane forwards, and it survives the control plane
sd-wan.recommended_action: Target four explicitly-separated planes (Manager cluster / redundant Controllers / redundant Validators / thin WAN edges); keep edges thin and policy central; rely on (and verify) OMP graceful restart so a controller outage never drops forwarding, and size the IPsec rekey timer to span the GR window.
sd-wan.citation: Orhan Ergun 'Evolving Technology: SD-WAN' deck + Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Design Guide; web-verified (Viptela -> Catalyst SD-WAN: Manager/Controller/Validator).

sd-wan.title: Let OMP to the Controller be the BGP-style overlay control plane -- routes, TLOCs and policy over one controller-rooted session, not a routing full-mesh
sd-wan.recommended_action: Place overlay routing under OMP to a redundant Controller cluster sited OUT of the data path; keep edges free of per-pair routing config; express path bias as OMP route-preference / TLOC-preference; keep site-local underlay routing (BGP/OSPF/connected) separate and redistribute into OMP deliberately.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Design Guide (OMP) + SD-WAN labs; web-verified that OMP is Cisco-proprietary, BGP-style, controller-rooted.

sd-wan.title: Recover the down OMP peering to vSmart before its 12-hour graceful-restart cache hides the loss
sd-wan.recommended_action: (1) Confirm the OMP state and scope with `show sdwan omp peers` — read the peer state (Up vs init-in-gr) and the R/I/S (received/installed/sent) counters; a peer stuck in graceful restart with stale routes is living on borrowed time. (2) Since OMP rides the control connection, first rule out a control-connection fault to that vSmart (history error code, reachability, certificate, NTP) — fix that and OMP typically re-establishes. (3) If the control connection is up but OMP is not converging, check OMP-layer health: hold-time/timer mismatch (Cisco recommends 300s hold time), graceful-restart configuration, and `send-path-limit` / route-count limits that can starve advertisement. (4) Use OMP vDiagnostics (auto-captures a snapshot on peering loss) to root-cause hello/timer/flap behavior. (5) Verify both vSmarts in the cluster are peered (redundancy restored) and that received/installed counts match the expected prefix set before re-baselining.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco — Routing Configuration Guide, Catalyst SD-WAN Releases 17.x: OMP and OMP graceful restart (OMP over DTLS/TLS, ACTIVE/STALE route states, default GR timer 43,200s/12h, EOR marker; recommended 300s hold time)

sd-wan.title: Migrate MPLS-to-SD-WAN per-site over a deliberate hybrid-coexistence period, with an explicit interworking point -- never a flag-day swap
sd-wan.recommended_action: Stand SD-WAN up in parallel with the live MPLS WAN; migrate sites in waves; retain the regional MPLS CEs/circuits and define an explicit MPLS<->SD-WAN transit/interworking point so all sites stay reachable throughout; validate (NRFU) and preserve rollback per wave; decommission MPLS only once the last wave is proven.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN migration guidance + SD-WAN labs; complements scenario-build-before-break-phased-cutover; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Model every WAN uplink as a TLOC (system-IP + color + encap) so one overlay rides MPLS, Internet and LTE/5G simultaneously and transport-agnostically
sd-wan.recommended_action: Define each uplink as a TLOC with a deliberate, consistent color taxonomy (private colors for MPLS/private, public colors for Internet/LTE/5G), default to IPsec encapsulation, BFD-track every transport, and use color + preference to express active/active vs active/standby; scope allow-service tightly on Internet TLOCs.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Design Guide (TLOC, colors, transport-independence) + SD-WAN labs; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Choose controller-based SD-WAN vs DMVPN/GETVPN/MPLS by whether transport-independence, app-aware SLA and central policy justify a controller
sd-wan.recommended_action: Adopt controller-based Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN when the estate needs transport-independent multi-transport blending, per-application SLA steering, central zero-touch policy at fleet scale, integrated branch security/DIA, or cloud/SaaS optimization; otherwise keep DMVPN/GETVPN where a simple, stable, few-site overlay with no-controller autonomy and lower cost suffices.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Design Guide + Orhan Ergun 'Evolving Technology: SD-WAN'; complements the KB's vpn-scale-dmvpn-getvpn-selection / wan-vpn-make-vs-buy; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Onboard WAN edges zero-touch on a mutual-trust chain -- allow-listed serial/chassis + a shared root CA + per-device certs, brokered by the Validator -- and encrypt by default
sd-wan.recommended_action: Choose the root-CA model deliberately (enterprise CA where internal PKI control is required, else Cisco PKI), distribute the root chain to every controller and edge, enforce one consistent organization-name, drive CSR/sign/install through the Manager, maintain the serial/chassis allow-list as a change-controlled artifact, and guarantee reliable NTP; treat the fabric as encrypted/authenticated by default and write transport firewall rules around the control-plane ports.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN onboarding / certificate trust (Validator allow-list + PKI; OMP-keyed IPsec) + SD-WAN labs; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Size a redundant, identical-policy Controller cluster off the data path, and bound fan-out by controller affinity
sd-wan.recommended_action: Deploy at least two geographically/cloud-diverse Controllers with byte-identical policy; configure each edge with redundant control connections; add Controllers toward the ~12 ceiling as edges grow past a single Controller's ~5000-connection limit; use controller-groups + per-edge max-controllers to bound fan-out; default to Cisco-cloud-hosted controllers unless sovereignty/air-gap/regulatory or a committed DC investment dictates on-prem.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controller scale/redundancy/affinity design; web-verified (~5000 conn/controller, controller groups, cloud-hosted vs on-prem).

sd-wan.title: Scale a large SD-WAN estate with Multi-Region Fabric (regions + border routers + core region 0), not one flat global full-mesh
sd-wan.recommended_action: For a large multi-region estate, design the overlay as Multi-Region Fabric: assign edges to regions (intra-region direct tunnels), deploy regional hubs as border routers forming core region 0, route inter-region traffic via border routers, and keep OMP/topology scope per region; avoid the extra roles until scale/geography/control-plane state actually demand them.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Multi-Region Fabric design; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Design SD-WAN and cloud security (SASE/SSE) as one converged fabric, and make the SIG breakout highly available
sd-wan.recommended_action: Design SD-WAN and the SSE (Umbrella SIG / Secure Access) as one fabric with intent authored once; provision at least two SIG tunnels per breakout site across multiple Umbrella data centres (active + backup), bind a layer-7 health tracker so failover follows real cloud reachability (not interface state), and define an explicit SIG-down fallback (on-box stack or controlled drop -- never silent uninspected egress).
sd-wan.citation: Cisco SASE / Umbrella SIG + Catalyst SD-WAN security design; web-verified.

sd-wan.title: Choose full-mesh vs hub-spoke vs regional topology by Controller policy, decoupled from physical transport
sd-wan.recommended_action: Use the default full-mesh only where direct any-to-any is justified and tunnel/OMP scale is acceptable (e.g. latency-critical inter-branch voice); otherwise express hub-and-spoke or a regional topology as centralized control policy (selective TLOC/route advertisement), and revisit it as the estate grows.
sd-wan.citation: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Design Guide (centralized control policy / topology) + SD-WAN labs; web-verified.

security.title: An FTD HA pair must hold a real Active/Standby split -- FMC is the authoritative HA verdict
security.recommended_action: Treat the degraded pair as a cutover blocker: confirm the failover/state link, unit health and the HA config in FMC, restore the standby to Standby, and (if intentionally suspended for maintenance) re-enable HA before the firewall is on the cutover path.
security.citation: Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense HA + FMC REST API (ftddevicehapairs currentStatus: Active/Standby/Failed/Not Detected/Disabled); standard stateful-HA design practice.

security.title: Defense-in-depth via modular, layered security zones — not perimeter-only
security.recommended_action: Segment into security modules/zones with layered per-module controls (edge firewall + iACL + IPS + L2 access protections + AAA), put the NMS in its own zone, run an asset/risk analysis to size controls to asset value, and use Private VLANs for intra-subnet isolation.
security.citation: CCDE Session 13 (defense-in-depth, zones, risk-driven controls, Private VLAN)

security.title: Re-establish the TrustSec environment-data download before cutover — without it the device has no SGT/SGACL policy to enforce
security.recommended_action: Restore the device→ISE policy channel, then re-pull data — carefully. (1) Read the current state with `show cts environment-data` (and the server list / last-download status) to see whether it never downloaded, is stale, or marked all servers dead. (2) Verify the transport and trust: ISE reachability (the REST/ERS path is TCP/9063), TLS handshake success, correct server IP/FQDN (a wrong or unresolvable domain name is a common cause), and that the device's CTS credentials/PAC match what ISE has under the network device's Advanced TrustSec settings — and that ISE permits REST API calls from this NAD's NAS-IP. (3) Confirm server-selection health: TrustSec prefers a configured static IP, falls back to the domain name, marks a non-responding server dead, fails the private list over to the public list, and only retries on the next request after marking servers alive — so a single dead-server entry can stall the whole pull. (4) Trigger/allow a refresh and confirm state returns to COMPLETE with the expected SGT table populated. Critical ordering caveat: do NOT manually refresh environment data while ISE is unreachable and the 802.1X links are in critical-authentication mode — a refresh that fails can wipe the existing policies; fix reachability first, then refresh. Only a COMPLETE download with the expected SGTs clears the segmentation gate.
security.citation: Cisco TrustSec Configuration Guide (Catalyst 9000) — 'SGACL and Environment Data Download over REST': environment-data contents and server failover (static-IP vs domain, private→public list, mark-dead/retry), TLS-handshake/HTTP-timeout/wrong-domain failure causes, ERS port 9063, and ISE NAD/NAS-IP REST prerequisites; with the Cisco TrustSec Troubleshooting Guide — `show cts environment-data` state=COMPLETE/Successful and the caution against refreshing env-data while ISE is unreachable in critical-auth mode (policies may clear).

security.title: A stateful firewall in the path needs an operational HA peer -- config-present is not redundancy
security.recommended_action: Treat the degraded pair as a cutover blocker: confirm the failover/state link is up, both units run compatible image + licensing, interface monitoring is healthy and config sync has completed, then restore the standby to Standby Ready BEFORE the firewall is on the cutover path. Where a firewall is intentionally standalone, design and document the accepted single-point-of-failure (or add a peer) -- do not leave a half-built pair.
security.citation: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA HA / Failover configuration guide (the show failover state machine: Active / Standby Ready / Failed / Not Detected / Disabled); standard stateful-HA practice.

security.title: Size the firewall above its OBSERVED peak -- a box denying or near its resource limits drops traffic
security.recommended_action: Size the replacement (or consolidated) firewall above the observed peak with headroom for growth AND failover (an HA pair must carry full load on one unit); re-evaluate per-context and per-class connection / embryonic limits; capture 'show resource usage' + 'show perfmon' at a real busy period as the sizing baseline and pin it into the NRFU acceptance.
security.citation: Cisco ASA performance & resource-management docs (show resource usage Denied / Limit); Cisco Secure Firewall sizing / capacity guidance.

security.title: Every FMC-managed FTD must stay connected + healthy -- a disconnected device can't be deployed-to
security.recommended_action: Confirm the device is powered, on-net and not mid-reboot/deploy; restore the FMC<->FTD management channel and clear the health alert before counting the device in-scope at cutover.
security.citation: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center REST API (devicerecords isConnected / healthStatus).

security.title: Keep the FMC management plane redundant -- a degraded FMC HA leaves the fleet unmanageable
security.recommended_action: Restore FMC HA synchronization and peer reachability (resolve any split-brain) before relying on the manager through the cutover; verify failover/promotion as part of NRFU.
security.citation: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center High Availability guide + REST API (fmchastatuses).

security.title: Keep every Fortinet FortiGate HA cluster in-sync and Health-OK (the firewall HA pair)
security.recommended_action: Identify the divergent objects ('diagnose sys ha checksum cluster' / the GUI HA widget), confirm identical firmware and ISDB / IPS / AV database versions on both units, then recalculate or force a resync until every member reads in-sync and Health is OK -- before the FortiGate is on the cutover path. Treat 'config-sync enable' as intent, not proof.
security.citation: Fortinet FortiOS Administration Guide -- HA, 'Check HA synchronization status' (get system ha status; in-sync / out-of-sync configuration checksums); Fortinet KB (HA checksum-mismatch troubleshooting); analogous to the Cisco ASA / FTD failover model

security.title: Keep every ISE deployment node Connected to the Primary Admin -- a partitioned node serves no AAA
security.recommended_action: Confirm the node is powered, on-net, time-synced (NTP) and that the PAN<->node path + certificates + replication are healthy; restore it to Connected before the access layer is cut over onto it. Ensure the switches' RADIUS server-groups list a reachable PSN so a single partition does not blackhole auth.
security.citation: Cisco ISE Administration / Deployment guide (deployment node status, replication); Cisco ISE Open API (GET /api/v1/deployment/node).

security.title: Deploy >=2 Policy Service Nodes (a node group) -- a single PSN is an authentication SPOF
security.recommended_action: Deploy at least two PSNs (a node group so session state survives a PSN loss); configure each switch's RADIUS server-group with both PSNs and dead-criteria/deadtime; size PSN count to the authenticating-endpoint scale. Confirm before cutover so the maintenance window cannot orphan the access layer.
security.citation: Cisco ISE Performance & Scalability / Deployment guide (PSN node groups, redundancy); Cisco TrustSec & SD-Access design guides (redundant PSN plane).

security.title: Keep every Juniper SRX chassis-cluster redundancy group ready to fail over (both nodes non-zero priority, monitoring clean)
security.recommended_action: Restore both nodes to a non-zero priority, clear the monitored interface/IP fault that decremented the priority, and confirm a healthy primary+secondary pair (plus the control link / fabric link and RG0 dampening) before the SRX is on the cutover path. Treat 'chassis cluster' in the config as intent, not proof -- verify the operational state.
security.citation: Juniper Junos OS Chassis Cluster (SRX) documentation -- redundancy-group failover & interface monitoring; Juniper KB19431 (priority-0 redundancy groups); analogous to the Cisco Secure Firewall (ASA / FTD) failover model

security.title: Use a dedicated, unused native VLAN on inter-switch trunks -- never VLAN 1
security.recommended_action: Assign a dedicated, unused native VLAN (not 1, not a data VLAN) on every inter-switch trunk and prune VLAN 1 from trunks; optionally enforce 'vlan dot1q tag native' so even the native VLAN is tagged. Apply it consistently on BOTH trunk ends (a native-VLAN mismatch is its own fault), and bake the chosen native VLAN into the target build template.
security.citation: Cisco L2 security hardening (dedicated native VLAN, 'vlan dot1q tag native', prune VLAN 1); 802.1Q double-tagging / VLAN-hopping; CIS Cisco benchmark trunk native-VLAN guidance.

security.title: Centralize AAA, authenticate routing adjacencies, and anti-spoof at the edge (uRPF/BCP38)
security.recommended_action: Deploy AAA (TACACS+ admin command-authz/accounting + RADIUS access) with RBAC/least-privilege and a guarded fallback; authenticate routing adjacencies and constrain BGP; implement BCP38 (uRPF + anti-bogon/RFC1918 ACLs) and infrastructure ACLs at the edge.
security.citation: CCDE Session 13 (AAA, routing auth, BCP38, iACLs); engine CIS axis (AAA/SSH detection)

security.title: Harden the device baseline: disable unneeded services, lock management, protect the control plane
security.recommended_action: Apply the hardening baseline (disable unneeded services, SSH-only + VTY ACL, password encryption, banners, timeouts, AAA for admin) and deploy CoPP + ICMP/feature rate-limits.
security.citation: CCDE Session 13 (device hardening, control plane); engine config-security/CIS axis

security.title: In the data center, add east-west micro-segmentation -- a north-south perimeter is necessary but not sufficient
security.recommended_action: Pair the north-south edge firewall with EAST-WEST enforcement: micro-segment with distributed/host-based firewalling, hypervisor (e.g. NSX) or fabric policy (e.g. ACI contracts), or steer inter-zone traffic through a firewall; default-deny intra-tier where feasible; drive policy from workload identity, not IP, under a least-privilege / zero-trust model.
security.citation: NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture (micro-segmentation limits lateral movement); Cisco SAFE Secure Data Center

security.title: Insert stateful firewalls on a SYMMETRIC path -- asymmetric routing breaks state, and HA is not free
security.recommended_action: Insert the firewall on the symmetric path (inline routed/transparent, or one-arm with PBR/VRF that forces both directions through it); avoid ECMP that lets return traffic bypass it; on HA pairs verify connection-state sync and divert/pin asymmetric flows to the active unit; test that failover preserves or gracefully re-establishes state.
security.citation: Cisco Secure Firewall routed/transparent & failover docs; ipSpace.net (Pepelnjak) 'Stateful Firewall Cluster High Availability Theater'; asymmetric-routing design guidance

security.title: Choose firewall mode and HA up front, account for context feature loss, and place IPS behind the firewall
security.recommended_action: Select mode to fit the insertion point and deploy failover/clustering; verify feature support before enabling contexts (keep single-context where dynamic routing/multicast is needed); place IPS behind the firewall with a hidden management interface and tuned signatures.
security.citation: CCDE Session 13 (firewall mode/HA, multi-context feature loss, IPS placement)

security.title: Segregate public services in a DMZ; use a screened-subnet (dual-firewall) edge for high assurance
security.recommended_action: Place public-facing services in a DMZ behind the edge firewall; for a high-assurance edge use a dual-firewall screened subnet (ideally different vendors/OSes so a single advisory can't breach both); permit only required DMZ<->inside flows; terminate remote-access VPN in its own zone, not straight onto the inside.
security.citation: Cisco SAFE Secure Edge; Cisco Firewall-and-IPS CVD; standard DMZ / screened-subnet design practice

security.title: Isolate the on-air-critical / high-value application tier -- do not leave it L3-reachable on the flat estate
security.recommended_action: Macro-segment the on-air-critical tiers into dedicated VRFs/zones (or a separate fabric segment) with enforced inter-zone policy -- gateway ACLs at minimum, a stateful firewall for IT<->broadcast flows, default-deny into the on-air path. In the EVPN target, a per-tenant VRF + L3VNI per critical tier with selective route leaking; keep PTP/ST-2110 multicast scoped within the tier.
security.citation: Cisco IP Fabric for Media (SMPTE ST 2110) design guide; Cisco SAFE secure segmentation; NIST SP 800-207 (segment high-value assets)

security.title: Harden the L2 access edge: port-security, DHCP snooping, DAI, IP Source Guard, storm-control, 802.1X
security.recommended_action: Standardize the access-edge bundle (port-security, DHCP snooping + IP Source Guard + DAI with trusted uplinks, storm-control, 802.1X with MAB/guest fallback); add RA Guard/DHCPv6 Guard for IPv6.
security.citation: CCDE Session 13/16 (L2 security suite, 802.1X/NAC); CCDE Session 15 (IPv6 RA/DHCPv6 Guard); engine CIS axis

security.title: Reconcile staged-but-undeployed FMC changes before cutover -- running config must equal intent
security.recommended_action: Reconcile each pending deployment BEFORE the cutover window -- deploy and re-validate, or explicitly defer with sign-off -- so the firewall's running state is known and intended at cutover; capture the deployment state in the NRFU baseline.
security.citation: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center REST API (deployabledevices) + change-management practice.

security.title: Keep the FMC at or ahead of every managed FTD's version -- a manager behind a device can't manage it
security.recommended_action: Upgrade the FMC to at least the highest managed-FTD version (following the supported FMC->FTD upgrade path) BEFORE relying on central management through the migration; sequence the migration's upgrades manager-first, devices-second.
security.citation: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center / Threat Defense compatibility + upgrade guides (FMC version must be >= managed device version).

security.title: Give the ISE PAN and MnT a Secondary -- a single Admin/Monitoring node loses management or visibility
security.recommended_action: Add a Secondary PAN (config/replication failover + promotion path) and a Secondary MnT (logging/reporting failover) so the control and logging planes survive a node loss; verify promotion and log continuity as part of NRFU before relying on the deployment at cutover.
security.citation: Cisco ISE Deployment / High Availability guide (PAN + MnT primary/secondary, promotion).

security.title: Filter the management plane (VTY/SNMP) to an explicit allowlist of NMS/NOC/VPN source prefixes -- not just SSH-only
security.recommended_action: Define a management source allowlist (NMS, monitoring, management VPN, NOC OOB) and enforce it with a per-line VTY access-class plus an SNMP-server ACL on every device tier; include the management-VRF path ('in vrf-also'); pair with SSH-only, exec-timeout and a legal login banner.
security.citation: EXPO2020 PSN Infra Hardening MOP (VTY access-class 'in vrf-also'; SNMP-server use-ipv4acl; exec-timeout); web-verified against Cisco IOS/IOS-XE management-plane hardening guidance.

segment-routing.title: Collapse LDP + RSVP-TE onto one IGP-distributed SID plane (SR-MPLS) to delete transport control-plane state
segment-routing.recommended_action: On an SR-capable target, run SR-MPLS over a single link-state IGP (IS-IS preferred for SP-scale multi-level + wide metrics; OSPF acceptable), advertise a prefix-SID per node loopback from a domain-wide consistent SRGB plus adjacency-SIDs per link, then decommission LDP and RSVP-TE once SR forwarding is verified end-to-end.
segment-routing.citation: RFC 8402 (Segment Routing Architecture) + RFC 8660 (SR-MPLS data plane) + Nick Russo CCIE-SP SR chapter; web-verified.

segment-routing.title: Reserve one non-overlapping SRGB and make it identical fleet-wide for deterministic end-to-end SR labels
segment-routing.recommended_action: Allocate one reserved SRGB that is identical on all SR nodes and provably disjoint from the dynamic MPLS label pool; document its lower bound and size as a domain-wide constant so prefix-SID indices map to the same absolute label on every hop.
segment-routing.citation: RFC 8402 + RFC 8660 (SR-MPLS data plane / SRGB) + Nick Russo CCIE-SP SR chapter; web-verified.

segment-routing.title: Use TI-LFA for 100% single-failure coverage on the actual post-convergence path, not best-effort LFA
segment-routing.recommended_action: Enable TI-LFA for link, node and SRLG protection across the SR IGP so every destination has a precomputed post-convergence repair SID-list; define SRLGs so fate-shared fibres/conduits are not each other's backup; verify the repair label-stack depth is within platform push limits before commit; pair with IGP micro-loop avoidance.
segment-routing.citation: RFC 9855 (Topology Independent Fast Reroute Using Segment Routing -- Standards Track, Oct 2025; supersedes the long-running draft) + RFC 8402; web-verified.

segment-routing.title: Migrate LDP to SR incrementally with an SR Mapping Server (SRMS) and contiguous loopback blocks
segment-routing.recommended_action: Stage the LDP->SR migration through an SRMS (advertise-local on the server, receive on clients) so SR and LDP islands coexist; carve the SRGB clear of LDP's dynamic labels and set SR-preferred label preference; pre-plan loopbacks as contiguous /32 blocks so a single mapping range covers many nodes.
segment-routing.citation: RFC 8661 (Segment Routing MPLS Interworking with LDP -- defines the SR Mapping Server) + Nick Russo CCIE-SP SR chapter; web-verified.

segment-routing.title: Encode SR-TE paths with prefix-SIDs for resilience; reserve adjacency-SID explicit paths for strict steering, and guard the no-validation blackhole
segment-routing.recommended_action: Default SR-TE forwarding to prefix-SID (node) paths for resilience and minimal stack depth; use adjacency-SID/strict-label paths only where exact link steering is required, and wherever label-explicit paths are used add active path validation/probing because the head-end will not detect a broken explicit path itself.
segment-routing.citation: RFC 9256 (SR Policy Architecture, updates RFC 8402) + the Cisco SR Phase-2 Solution Test Report (SR-TE caveats); web-verified.

sp-l2vpn.title: Treat a VPLS instance as one WAN-wide flood / MAC-learning domain and bound it with limits + snooping
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: Right-size the emulated LAN: set per-VFI MAC-address-table limits with an explicit unknown-MAC action, enable IGMP/PIM snooping to constrain multicast flooding, control BPDUs at the access edge, and prefer L3VPN or point-to-point VPWS where multipoint L2 reach is not actually required.
sp-l2vpn.citation: RFC 4761 (VPLS using BGP) / RFC 4762 (VPLS using LDP) + Cisco MPLS L2/L3-VPN course; web-verified.

sp-l2vpn.title: Carry point-to-point E-Line over EVPN-VPWS (no PW signaling, no MAC learning) instead of LDP pseudowires
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: When designing or modernizing point-to-point Ethernet (E-Line) transport, specify EVPN-VPWS (RFC 8214) as the service type: one EVI per service with a VPWS service ID (Ethernet-tag/AC-ID), route-targets to scope reachability, and no MAC advertisement. Reserve LDP/BGP-AD pseudowires only for interop with PE nodes that cannot run EVPN.
sp-l2vpn.citation: IETF RFC 8214, 'Virtual Private Wire Service Support in Ethernet VPN' (Aug 2017); Cisco 'EVPN Virtual Private Wire Service (VPWS) -- E-Line Service', IOS XR L2VPN/EVPN Configuration Guide.

sp-l2vpn.title: Coordinate a redundant PW set so both PE endpoints select the SAME single active pseudowire
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: For every redundant pseudowire set, specify the coordination mode (independent vs master/slave), an explicit per-PW precedence or primary/secondary order, and the revertive policy; verify both endpoints agree on the single active member before cutover so the standby PW is hot-standby, not a second active path.
sp-l2vpn.citation: IETF RFC 6718 (Pseudowire Redundancy) and RFC 6870 (Pseudowire Preferential Forwarding Status Bit).

sp-l2vpn.title: Keep multihoming Single-Active until the last VPLS PE of an instance is gone; defer EVPN all-active to the EVPN-only end state
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: In the VPLS-to-EVPN HLD/MOP, gate All-Active EVPN multihoming behind 'instance fully EVPN'. Configure Single-Active on every multihomed segment that still shares an instance with a VPLS PE, and schedule the per-ES flip to All-Active as an explicit post-migration step, not as part of initial EVPN turn-up.
sp-l2vpn.citation: IETF RFC 8560 (All-Active redundancy not applicable to VPLS coexistence -- MUST use Single-Active); RFC 7432 EVPN Ethernet-Segment redundancy modes.

sp-l2vpn.title: Migrate legacy VPLS/LDP-VPWS to EVPN one PE at a time via dual-stack coexistence; collapse fan-out with FXC service-multiplexing only after
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: Plan an SP L2VPN modernization as: (a) per-PE dual-stack EVPN-VPWS+legacy-VPWS coexistence over the existing MPLS core, migrating one AC/PE pair at a time with rollback to the legacy PW; then (b) where AC fan-out is high, adopt FXC (single VPWS service ID, normalized VIDs not signaled) to cap BGP route count. Verify route-count and convergence at each step.
sp-l2vpn.citation: Cisco 'Migration of VPLS and VPWS Networks to EVPN' (IOS XR EVPN Configuration Guide); IETF RFC 9744, 'EVPN VPWS Flexible Cross-Connect (FXC) Service' (Mar 2025).

sp-l2vpn.title: Migrate VPLS to EVPN seamlessly per-VPN-instance with RFC 8560 integration, not a flag-day re-provision
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: When the target state is BGP-EVPN over an MPLS/SR core that today runs VPLS, plan the cutover as RFC 8560 seamless integration: enable EVPN on PEs incrementally per VPN instance, let each EVPN PE bridge to remaining VPLS PEs via pseudowires, validate the union domain, then retire VPLS per instance. Do not schedule one global VPLS-to-EVPN flag day.
sp-l2vpn.citation: IETF RFC 8560 (Seamless Integration of EVPN with VPLS and their PBB Equivalents, 2019); Cisco IOS XR EVPN Configuration Guide, 'Seamless Migration of VPLS Network to EVPN'.

sp-l2vpn.title: Pin the service PW to a transport path (preferred-path) and drive fast failover with PW-status / MAC-withdrawal signalling
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: Bind each protected PW to a preferred-path transport tunnel with an explicit fallback policy, and ensure failover propagation is enabled (PW status signalling plus MAC-withdrawal on VPLS/multipoint members) so remote PEs flush stale MACs and reconverge onto the new active PW instead of black-holing.
sp-l2vpn.citation: Cisco MPLS Layer 2 VPNs Configuration Guide -- L2VPN Pseudowire Redundancy & preferred-path (pseudowire-class); VPLS MAC Address Withdrawal (LDP MAC-list TLV), consistent with RFC 6870 PW status procedures.

sp-l2vpn.title: Select the EVPN Ethernet-Segment redundancy mode (all-active / single-active / port-active) from the access constraint
sp-l2vpn.recommended_action: For each multihomed segment, name the redundancy mode and justify it: all-active only where the CE presents one cross-PE LACP LAG and per-flow LB is wanted; single-active where the CE can't LAG or per-service carving is required; port-active where bundle-level deterministic active/standby (QoS/ordering) is needed. Require synchronized LACP parameters across the PE pair in every case.
sp-l2vpn.citation: IETF RFC 7432 (All-Active/Single-Active redundancy); IETF RFC 9786 (EVPN Port-Active Redundancy Mode, Jun 2025); Cisco IOS XE MPLS Configuration Guide, CE EVPN Multihoming.

sp-mpls.title: Separate the attachment-circuit fault from the pseudowire/underlay fault before declaring the L2 circuit cut
sp-mpls.recommended_action: (1) Read the state first: `show mpls l2transport vc <id> detail` (IOS XR: `show l2vpn xconnect detail`) and split the symptom — is the local AC down, is the remote VC label missing (peer/underlay problem), or are both labels present but the PW still down (parameter mismatch)? (2) Fix the attachment circuit if the AC is down — the customer-facing interface/EFP, its encapsulation, and link/line-protocol state — because no PW comes up over a dead AC. (3) Reconcile the signaling parameters end-to-end: the VC-ID/PW-ID and PW type must match on both PEs, and MTU/encapsulation must agree (note IOS XR counts the L2 header in its MTU, a frequent IOS-XE↔IOS-XR mismatch); confirm `encapsulation mpls`/pw-class is present. (4) If the AC is up and parameters match but the remote VC label is absent, drop to the underlay: confirm the targeted LDP session to the peer is up and the transport LSP to the peer loopback is label-switched — `show mpls ldp neighbor`, `show mpls forwarding-table <peer-/32>`, and validate with a VCCV/PW ping (`ping mpls pseudowire …`). (5) Remediate the layer that failed and re-verify the PW shows UP/UP (AC up, PW up) before re-baselining.
sp-mpls.citation: RFC 4447 (Pseudowire Setup and Maintenance Using LDP) — targeted LDP, PWid FEC/VC-ID match, VC label, PW Status TLV, PSN-tunnel dependency; and Cisco 'Understand MPLS L2VPN Pseudowire' (Doc ID 213238)

sp-mpls.title: Triage the L3VPN underlay before the VPNv4 overlay, then prove the two-label path before cutover
sp-mpls.recommended_action: Follow Cisco's top-down-then-underlay sequence. (1) Establish the control plane: `show bgp vpnv4 unicast all summary` (IOS XR: `show bgp vpnv4 unicast summary`) — is the PE-PE/RR session Established and is the VPNv4/MP-BGP address family activated with send-community extended? (2) Confirm policy: the prefix is present with the right RD and its RTs match the remote VRF's import list — `show bgp vpnv4 unicast all <prefix>` and `show vrf <name>` for import/export RTs; a one-sided RT edit is the classic silent break. (3) Confirm the route landed in the VRF and carries a VPN label — `show ip route vrf <name>` and `show bgp vpnv4 unicast all tags` / `show ip cef vrf <name> <prefix> detail`. (4) Now prove the UNDERLAY the overlay depends on: is the remote PE's BGP-next-hop /32 reachable AND label-switched end-to-end? `show mpls forwarding-table <nexthop-/32>` on the ingress PE and at each P hop, then validate the LSP with `ping mpls ipv4 <nexthop>/32` (LSP ping). The order is deliberate: a VPNv4 symptom is frequently an LDP/IGP fault one layer down (this is why the LDP-session-down principle is a prerequisite). (5) Remediate the layer that actually failed — re-peer/activate AF, re-align RTs, or fix the transport LSP — and only then re-baseline.
sp-mpls.citation: RFC 4364 (BGP/MPLS IP VPNs) — VPNv4 routes, RD/RT, two-level label stack, PE-reachability requirement; and Cisco 'How to Troubleshoot the MPLS VPN' (Doc ID 13734) for the show-command sequence

sp-mpls.title: Restore the down LDP session before baselining or cutting over the MPLS underlay
sp-mpls.recommended_action: Work bottom-up. (1) Confirm the IGP underneath the session is up and the peer's transport address / router-ID loopback is in the RIB — `show mpls ldp neighbor` / `show mpls ldp discovery` (IOS XR: `show mpls ldp neighbor brief`) to see whether you are stuck at Hello/discovery or at session establishment. (2) If discovery is fine but the TCP session won't form, verify L3 reachability to the LDP transport address and that nothing blocks TCP/646 or has lowered path MTU; check `mpls ldp router-id`/transport-address pinning and that label protocol is enabled on the interface. (3) Inspect label exchange with `show mpls ldp bindings` / `show mpls forwarding-table` to confirm bindings return. (4) Bounce only the affected adjacency with `clear mpls ldp neighbor <ip>` (never restart the LDP process under traffic). (5) Harden against recurrence before cutover: enable LDP-IGP synchronization so the IGP advertises max-metric on a link until LDP is converged (prevents the blackhole), and LDP session protection so a backup targeted-hello adjacency holds the session and its label bindings up across a direct-link flap.
sp-mpls.citation: RFC 5036 (LDP Specification) — sessions, KeepAlive/holdtime, label distribution; and Cisco MPLS Configuration Guide — MPLS LDP IGP Synchronization (blackhole prevention)

sp-mpls.title: Choose the inter-AS L3VPN handoff (Option A/B/C, plus CsC) by the ASBR-state vs scale vs trust tradeoff
sp-mpls.recommended_action: Select by requirement: Option A when isolation/simplicity dominate and VPN count is low; Option B for moderate scale with VPN state acceptable at the border (retain route-targets across the ASBR); Option C / CsC when many VPNs + a provider hierarchy demand loopback-to-loopback label paths and the providers accept the coordination (Option C preserves the originating PE next-hop; CsC exchanges labels via BGP-LU at the boundary).
sp-mpls.citation: RFC 4364 §10 (inter-AS L3VPN Options a/b/c) + Orhan Ergun CCIE-SP inter-AS / CsC workbooks; web-verified.

sp-mpls.title: Treat the inter-AS / inter-provider edge as untrusted: explicit inbound + outbound route-policy, never pass-all
sp-mpls.recommended_action: At every inter-AS edge bind explicit, named inbound AND outbound route-policies that permit only the intended prefixes/loopbacks and (for VPNv4) only the intended route-targets; never ship a permit-any; pair the filter with prefix-count limits / max-prefix on the neighbour.
sp-mpls.citation: RFC 4364 §10 (inter-provider) + Orhan Ergun CCIE-SP inter-AS lab (IOS-XR sends/accepts nothing until a route-policy is applied); web-verified.

sp-mpls.title: Plan the Route Distinguisher to keep overlapping customer prefixes distinct (and per-PE-unique where VPN path diversity is needed)
sp-mpls.recommended_action: Assign each VRF an explicit, planned RD (do not rely on the auto/default RD); keep RD allocation in an addressing/RD plan; where a VRF is anchored on two+ PEs and VPN path redundancy/multipath is required, allocate a distinct RD per PE (or use BGP Add-Path on the RR) so the RR retains all paths.
sp-mpls.citation: RFC 4364 (VPN-IPv4 = 8-byte RD + 4-byte IPv4) + Cisco MPLS L2/L3-VPN course; web-verified.

sp-mpls.title: Engineer L3VPN connectivity topology with Route-Target import/export, not with the RD
sp-mpls.recommended_action: Design the VPN connectivity matrix explicitly as an RT import/export plan -- symmetric RTs for any-to-any, hub-exports/spoke-imports (and the inverse) for hub-and-spoke, a dedicated shared-services RT for controlled extranet -- and document the intended topology alongside the RT scheme so membership cannot drift.
sp-mpls.citation: RFC 4364 (Route-Target extended community governs VRF import/export) + Cisco MPLS L2/L3-VPN course; web-verified.

sp-mpls.title: Use BGP labeled-unicast to stitch one end-to-end LSP across a domain/AS boundary with no shared IGP/LDP
sp-mpls.recommended_action: Scope IGP+LDP inside each domain; add a BGP labeled-unicast session across the seam (eBGP between border nodes and the remote PE) advertising only the service/transport endpoints with labels for a contiguous end-to-end LSP; carry the customer service as a pseudowire/VPN over it.
sp-mpls.citation: BGP-LU on the TIM OPM network (Overview / Topology / Packet forwarding); web-verified against RFC 8277 (Using BGP to Bind MPLS Labels to Address Prefixes, obsoletes RFC 3107).

sp-mvpn.title: Choose the provider tunnel and the C-multicast signalling plane as two independent decisions
sp-mvpn.recommended_action: State the P-tunnel and the C-multicast signalling as SEPARATE selections in the HLD, each justified against its own driver (core protection/state for the tunnel; PE/adjacency scale for the signalling) -- never adopt a profile number as a bundle.
sp-mvpn.citation: RFC 6513 (Multicast in MPLS/BGP IP VPNs framework) + RFC 6514 (BGP encodings / MCAST-VPN A-D + C-multicast routes); web-verified.

sp-mvpn.title: Default to mLDP P-tunnels for MVPN; reserve RSVP-TE P2MP for bandwidth-guaranteed few-source trees (and ride mLDP over TE when you need both)
sp-mvpn.recommended_action: In the target-state MVPN design, set mLDP as the default provider-tunnel type fleet-wide and justify any RSVP-TE P2MP island against a concrete bandwidth-reservation/few-source-video driver; if TE or guaranteed-path is required under an otherwise-mLDP design, document the mLDP-over-RSVP-TE-tunnel steering option and the FRR model (TI-LFA/MoFRR for mLDP) instead of head-end P2MP-TE backup trees. Engine cannot verify the provider core, so emit this as advisory doctrine, not a fired detector.
sp-mvpn.citation: Cisco, 'Core of Multicast VPNs: Rationale for Using mLDP' (whitepaper C11-598929); NANOG 49, 'Introduction to Label-Switched Multicast: P2MP-TE & mLDP'; RFC 9860 'Multicast-Only Fast Reroute (MoFRR) Based on TI-LFA' (Informational, Oct 2025)

sp-mvpn.title: Minimize provider-core tree state with on-demand / partitioned MDT (S-PMSI built only between PEs that actually exchange traffic) instead of a full-mesh default MDT
sp-mvpn.recommended_action: For a target-state MVPN, prefer an on-demand selective-tree model (partitioned MDT / S-PMSI-on-demand, Profile 14-style) over a full-mesh always-on default MDT when PE count or source/receiver sparsity makes per-PE tree state the scaling bottleneck; size the expected tree count from the source-to-interested-receiver matrix, not from PE count. Advisory only -- the engine has no view of the provider MDT plane.
sp-mvpn.citation: Cisco, 'IP Multicast: MVPN Configuration Guide -- MVPN mLDP Partitioned MDT' (IOS XE 17.1.x); Cisco, 'Configure mVPN Profiles within Cisco IOS XR' (Doc 200512, Profile 14 Partitioned MDT)

sp-mvpn.title: Prefer mLDP (label-switched P-tunnels) over PIM-GRE to keep PIM and per-VPN state out of the core
sp-mvpn.recommended_action: Specify mLDP P2MP (and MP2MP where a shared tree fits) as the default P-tunnel; use a data-MDT to move high-rate streams off the default tree; reserve PIM-GRE for interop with legacy PEs or a non-MPLS core, documenting the core-state + protection consequences if it is retained.
sp-mvpn.citation: RFC 6388 (mLDP -- LDP extensions for P2MP/MP2MP LSPs) + RFC 6037 (Cisco draft-Rosen MVPN, informational); web-verified.

sp-mvpn.title: Set the data-MDT threshold (and its hold-down) as an explicit bandwidth-vs-core-state trade-off, not a default
sp-mvpn.recommended_action: Document, per multicast VRF, the data-MDT threshold and data-holddown (switch-back) timer, and justify the value against the C-source rate distribution and the core's per-router multicast-state budget. Avoid both extremes: an unset threshold (heavy flows flood all PEs) and an aggressively low one (state explosion + tree flapping on bursty sources). Re-evaluate the threshold when source bandwidth profiles change rather than leaving an inherited default.
sp-mvpn.citation: RFC 6037 (Rosen) Data-MDT (SP-owned bandwidth-vs-P-router-state tradeoff); RFC 6513 (Selective vs Inclusive PMSI); Cisco IP Multicast: MVPN Configuration Guide (mdt data threshold, data holddown / switchover)

sp-transport.title: Never summarize PE BGP-next-hop loopbacks in the core IGP -- VPN/LSP label resolution needs the exact /32
sp-transport.recommended_action: Exclude PE / PE-next-hop loopbacks from any core IGP summarization or filtering; carry them as exact host routes end-to-end (or stitch summarized domains with BGP-LU); summarize only customer / infrastructure prefixes, and verify label/LSP resolution to each PE loopback in the design's NRFU plan.
sp-transport.citation: RFC 4364 (BGP/MPLS IP VPNs -- backbone IGP must carry a host route to each LSP egress PE) + Cisco MPLS L2/L3-VPN troubleshooting course; web-verified.

sp-transport.title: Prefer SR-TE stateless source-routed policies over RSVP-TE soft-state for scalable traffic engineering
sp-transport.recommended_action: Default new TE to SR-TE (head-end-imposed segment lists, stateless midpoints) for scale and operational simplicity; retain or overlay RSVP-TE only on the specific paths that need bandwidth admission / guaranteed reservations the stateless model cannot provide.
sp-transport.citation: RFC 9256 (SR Policy = ordered segment list, source-routed) + Nick Russo CCIE-SP; web-verified.

sp-transport.title: Centralise SR-TE with a stateful PCE over PCEP + BGP-LS, but gate the controller on feature maturity and validate paths yourself
sp-transport.recommended_action: Architect SR-TE with a stateful PCE (PCE-initiated LSPs over PCEP) fed by BGP-LS, selecting only a controller whose required SR-TE features are GA; add active liveness/path validation (independent probing) because PCE/head-end state can show 'up' across a failed hop; design controller redundancy so it is not a single point of failure.
sp-transport.citation: RFC 8664 (PCEP extensions for SR) + RFC 9552 (BGP-LS, obsoletes RFC 7752) + RFC 9256 + the Cisco SR Phase-2 Test Report (SDN/PCE defects); web-verified.

sp-transport.title: Select the physical transport topology (ring / hub-spoke / partial-mesh / full-mesh) from the role each layer serves
sp-transport.recommended_action: Map each transport layer to a topology by its dominant requirement (cost-sensitive collection -> ring + engineered FRR; concentration point -> hub-and-spoke + SPOF mitigation; core/aggregation -> partial-mesh; latency/diversity-critical -> full-mesh); never apply one topology uniformly across all layers.
sp-transport.citation: Orhan Ergun CCIE-SP design-comparison chart (ring vs hub-spoke vs partial-mesh vs full-mesh); complements topology-triangles-not-squares-rings (the convergence-geometry rule).

storage-fabric.title: Cross-VSAN storage access: route with Inter-VSAN Routing, never merge the two VSANs
storage-fabric.recommended_action: In the design, satisfy any cross-VSAN storage requirement with IVR (virtual-domain + pWWN-scoped IVR zones + service groups), explicitly forbidding a VSAN merge as the means of sharing a target; document each IVR adjacency as a reviewed exception to default VSAN isolation.
storage-fabric.citation: Cisco MDS 9000 Series Inter-VSAN Routing Configuration Guide (Basic Inter-VSAN Routing Configuration: IVR virtual domain, IVR zones, CFS-distributed IVR topology, service groups)

storage-fabric.title: Enforce SAN zoning with enhanced zoning, pWWN device-aliases and smart zoning -- hard, init-to-target-only, name-based
storage-fabric.recommended_action: In the LLD mandate enhanced zoning (basic only for interop), pWWN device-alias enhanced mode with 1:1 mapping, and smart zoning for init-to-target-only adjacency; prohibit soft/name-server-only enforcement and (domain,port) member identity for production hosts.
storage-fabric.citation: Cisco MDS 9000 Series Fabric Configuration Guide (Configuring and Managing Zones; Distributing Device Alias Services); Cisco Community 'Cisco MDS SAN Zoning Best Practices' (enhanced zoning, device-alias enhanced mode, smart zoning, hard vs soft)

storage-fabric.title: Isolate FC fabrics into VSANs and zone by stable WWN identity (device-alias / smart-zoning), never by switch port
storage-fabric.recommended_action: Design one VSAN per logical fabric/tenant with an explicitly allocated, non-default domain-ID per VSAN; zone exclusively by pWWN via device-aliases under a documented naming standard; default to single-initiator/single-target zones (or smart zoning to collapse the zone count without losing that property); keep the default VSAN 1 unused for production traffic.
storage-fabric.citation: Cisco MDS 9000 Series Fabric Configuration Guide (Configuring and Managing Zones; Configuring and Managing VSANs); Cisco Community 'Cisco MDS SAN Zoning Best Practices'

storage-fabric.title: RoCEv2 / NVMe-oF demands an engineered lossless fabric: dedicated no-drop PFC class + ECN/WRED (DCQCN) + jumbo MTU, kept inside a pod
storage-fabric.recommended_action: When RoCEv2/NVMe-oF (or an AI/ML RDMA tier) is the target, specify the lossless contract explicitly: a dedicated no-drop CoS with PFC on the RoCEv2 priority, ECN/WRED thresholds at leaf and spine for DCQCN, end-to-end jumbo MTU on every hop, and a pod-bounded RoCEv2 domain; flag any plan that runs RDMA storage over a best-effort or partially-configured fabric as a design risk.
storage-fabric.citation: Cisco 'Data Center Networking Blueprint for AI/ML Applications' and 'RoCE Storage Implementation over NX-OS VXLAN Fabrics' (PFC + WRED-ECN no-drop class); NVIDIA RoCE-over-lossless-fabric (PFC+ECN) guide; DCQCN (SIGCOMM 2015)

storage-fabric.title: Select core-edge vs collapsed-core SAN topology and size ISLs to an explicit storage-to-host fan-out / oversubscription budget
storage-fabric.recommended_action: Document the target fan-out ratio per storage platform and derive the host-edge ISL port-channel width from it (e.g. an 8:1 budget on a given host-edge defines required ISL Gbps to the core); collapse to a single-tier core only where the director pair holds the full port count with growth headroom; bundle every edge-core link set into one FC port-channel spanning line cards for resilience, and keep the A/B fabrics symmetric in this sizing.
storage-fabric.citation: Cisco Large SAN Design Best Practices (MDS 9710/9700 directors) white paper; Cisco MDS 9000 Interfaces Configuration Guide (Configuring Port Channels)

storage-fabric.title: Treat FC fabric-merge (E-port/ISL bring-up) as a change gate: pre-reconcile zoneset and domain-ID conflicts or the merging fabric isolates
storage-fabric.recommended_action: Before enabling any new ISL/E-port between fabrics, capture and diff both sides' active zoneset, VSAN list and domain-ID allocation; resolve domain-ID overlaps (static, non-conflicting allocation) and default-zone/zoneset policy mismatches first; stage the merge in a maintenance window with a defined rollback (shut the E-port) and verify the merged fabric's zoneset activated cleanly and no switch isolated.
storage-fabric.citation: Cisco MDS 9000 Series Fabric Configuration Guide (zone-merge / zoneset-activation behavior); Cisco MDS 9000 Interfaces Configuration Guide (E-port/TE-port and port-channel formation)

vpn.title: Scale site-to-site VPN with DMVPN (or GETVPN on a private core), and select the overlay by transport/security need
vpn.recommended_action: Adopt DMVPN for large Internet-backed fan-outs (mGRE/NHRP/IPsec, spoke stubs); use GETVPN only on private/MPLS transport with no NAT; pick the simplest overlay that satisfies transport+security (GRE/mGRE for IPv6 with no crypto need; add IPsec only when confidentiality is required); never propose provider MPLS VPN over the public Internet.
vpn.citation: CCDE Session 14 (DMVPN/GETVPN/GRE-IPsec/VTI); CCDE scenarios (overlay selection, DMVPN vs GETVPN)

vpn.title: Choose WAN/overlay routing for adjacency scale, wrap IPsec in GRE/VTI for routing+multicast, and decide split-tunneling explicitly
vpn.recommended_action: Select the overlay IGP by adjacency scale and family (EIGRP moderate, BGP high/policy), stub the spokes, size hub head-ends to the supported neighbour count; wrap IPsec in GRE/VTI for routing/multicast with QoS pre-classify; default to tunnel-all and allow split-tunnel only on trusted hardware.
vpn.citation: CCDE Session 14 (GRE/VTI, IP pre-classify, split-tunnel); CCDE scenario (EIGRP/BGP adjacency-scale, spoke stubs)

wan.title: Restore the down DMVPN/NHRP spoke before treating the overlay topology as complete
wan.recommended_action: Work the dependency chain bottom-up, exactly as Cisco's DMVPN troubleshooting method prescribes — verify GRE/NHRP before blaming IPsec. (1) On the hub, run 'show dmvpn detail' and 'show ip nhrp nhs detail' to confirm whether the spoke is registered and in which state (UP vs NHRP/IKE); a peer that never reaches UP is a registration failure, one that flaps points at holdtime/keepalive or an unstable underlay. (2) Confirm underlay reachability of the spoke's NBMA address and that IKE/IPsec transport (UDP 500/4500, ESP) is permitted end-to-end — a NAT device newly in path or an ACL on the transport is the classic cause. (3) Validate the GRE/tunnel layer in isolation (tunnel source/destination, NHRP network-id, authentication, and the NHS address the spoke is configured to register to); Cisco's guidance is to prove the GRE tunnel works before layering IPsec. (4) Only then descend into the crypto session (see ipsec-crypto-session-down) if NHRP registration is initiating but the protected session will not establish. (5) Re-verify with 'show dmvpn detail' that the peer reaches UP and that NHRP shortcuts re-form before clearing the finding.
wan.citation: Cisco — Troubleshoot Common DMVPN Issues (NHRP registration/state, 'verify the GRE tunnels work fine without IPsec encryption', show dmvpn detail / show ip nhrp nhs detail)

wan.title: Re-establish the down IPsec/IKE session before baselining any traffic that depends on the encrypted path
wan.recommended_action: Diagnose top of the stack down, isolating the failing phase before changing config. (1) 'show crypto session [detail]' for a single per-peer view of session status and whether SAs are active; (2) 'show crypto isakmp sa' (IKEv1) / 'show crypto ikev2 sa' to confirm Phase 1 — if it is not MM_ACTIVE/established the problem is Phase 1: verify the peer is reachable and UDP 500/4500 + ESP are permitted end-to-end, then check matching Phase 1 policy (encryption/hash/DH/lifetime), the pre-shared key, and peer identity/PKI; (3) if Phase 1 is up but Phase 2 is not, 'show crypto ipsec sa' and confirm the transform sets match exactly and the crypto ACLs mirror each other on both peers (non-reversible ACLs cause the proxy-ID mismatch that blocks Phase 2); (4) prove the data plane by checking that encaps and decaps both increment — increment in only one direction indicates an asymmetric/return-path or one-sided ACL fault; (5) where state is stale or flapping, 'clear crypto isakmp' / 'clear crypto sa' to force a clean renegotiation, using debug only when the static checks do not localize the fault. Re-verify encaps/decaps before clearing the finding.
wan.citation: Cisco — Understand and Use Debug Commands to Troubleshoot IPsec (IKE Phase 1/Phase 2 states, proxy-ID/transform/crypto-ACL mismatch, clear crypto, encaps/decaps verification)

wan-vpn.title: When MPLS/VPN forces BGP into the design, run BGP end-to-end instead of redistribution -- and plan MTU headroom before any label/tunnel
wan-vpn.recommended_action: When combining MPLS/VPN with any other WAN connectivity, adopt BGP as the single WAN routing protocol end-to-end instead of multiplying redistribution boundaries, reserving the IGP for intra-site reachability and BGP-next-hop resolution and using communities/local-pref/MED for path selection; if OSPF must stay, keep the PE-CE link in area 0, anticipate the ABR/external behavior, add sham-links only with SP coordination, avoid multi-process-plus-mutual-redistribution failover, and use EIGRP SoO for multihomed sites. Before enabling any encapsulation, compute the worst-case header stack and set MTU accordingly (bump core/transit-switch MTU to jumbo/baby-jumbo, or clamp PE-CE/access MTU / MSS), audit L2 switches on the path for jumbo support and current MTU, and record MTU as an explicit pre-cutover gate.
wan-vpn.citation: ipSpace.net 'Integrating Internet VPN with MPLS/VPN WAN' / 'Combining DMVPN and MPLS VPN' / 'Choose the Optimal VPN Service' (Pepelnjak) and NIL 'Enterprise MPLS/VPN Deployment' (PE-CE redistribution, OSPF-as-PE-CE traps, core MTU/jumbo-frames guidance)

wan-vpn.title: Choose provider-vs-self-built VPN by who owns convergence, and make SP-controlled behaviors test-before-buy acceptance criteria
