wan-vpn.recommended_action: Make ownership-of-convergence-and-core an explicit scored criterion alongside cost: prefer provider L3VPN where the SP is competent and the priority is maximum outsourcing of a large simple network; build a customer overlay (optionally over the provider's IP service to also fix a weak SP) where retaining routing/convergence control, avoiding lock-in or spanning multiple providers matters; document SP competence as a stated assumption. Build a test-before-buy/PoC gate: verify PE-to-CE load-sharing and automatic backup (or mandate BGP PE-CE), confirm end-to-end transparency (STP/BPDU/CDP/LACP, jumbo MTU, QoS marking, remote link-loss signaling), and capture each as a pass/fail acceptance criterion.
wan-vpn.citation: ipSpace.net 'Choose the Optimal VPN Service' (Pepelnjak) -- MPLS/VPN benefits/drawbacks, decision guidelines, 'Test-before-buy!' load-sharing/backup/transparency slides; RFC 4271 (BGP-4)

wireless.title: Engineer the roam, not just the cell: combine 802.11k/v steering with 802.11r Fast Transition (or OKC) to hold the handoff under the real-time budget
wireless.recommended_action: On roam-sensitive SSIDs enable 802.11k neighbor lists + 802.11v BSS-transition steering, add 802.11r FT (or OKC / adaptive-11r for mixed fleets) to pre-authenticate; keep the roam within an L2 domain or design L3 roaming via the WLC/fabric.
wireless.citation: Cisco wireless roaming design (802.11r/k/v, OKC); web-verified.

wireless.title: Design RF for capacity by shrinking cells (not coverage by raising power); let RRM own channel/power and validate with a survey chain
wireless.recommended_action: For high density, lower AP power + add APs to shrink cells, raise RX-SOP, disable lowest legacy rates, target ~15-20% overlap, keep placement uniform; enable DCA/TPC/coverage-hole + FRA on XOR radios; choose narrow (20/40MHz) channel width in density; run predictive -> passive -> active surveys + a post-install validation.
wireless.citation: Cisco High-Density Wi-Fi / RRM design guidance; web-verified.

wireless.title: Pick the WLC deployment model (centralized local-mode / FlexConnect / embedded / cloud) from branch survivability and WAN latency
wireless.recommended_action: Keep campus on centralized local-mode within a low-latency LAN; default branches with unreliable or >100ms WAN to FlexConnect local-switching + local authentication (survive Standalone); use embedded EWC / cloud-managed for small or highly-distributed sites.
wireless.citation: Cisco Enterprise Wireless / Catalyst 9800 Design Guide (local-mode vs FlexConnect, CAPWAP); web-verified.

wireless.title: Make WPA3 + PMF the WLAN baseline (OWE for guest, 6GHz WPA3-only with SAE H2E); authenticate corporate with 802.1X/EAP-TLS to ISE
wireless.recommended_action: Adopt WPA3 + mandatory PMF as the personal/enterprise baseline, Enhanced-Open (OWE) for guest, 6GHz strictly WPA3-only with SAE H2E; authenticate managed WLAN with 802.1X to a redundant ISE plane, prefer EAP-TLS; scope WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit to CNSA-required networks; treat transition-mode SSIDs as temporary.
wireless.citation: Wi-Fi Alliance WPA3 + Cisco WLAN security design (OWE, SAE H2E, 802.1X/EAP-TLS, ISE); web-verified.

wireless.title: Treat CAPWAP as a split control/data plane with a hard AP-to-WLC latency budget and a mandatory DTLS control channel
wireless.recommended_action: Keep AP-to-WLC RTT inside ~300ms (aim < ~100ms for centralized); priority-queue CAPWAP control (UDP 5246) across the path; size the WLC + its uplink for the aggregate local-mode data tunnel; move high-latency/unreliable branches to FlexConnect local-switching rather than stretching CAPWAP.
wireless.citation: Cisco CAPWAP / Catalyst 9800 design (control UDP 5246 DTLS, data 5247, RTT budget); web-verified.

wireless.title: Exploit Wi-Fi 6/6E airtime efficiency (OFDMA/MU-MIMO/BSS-color/TWT) in dense cells; treat Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) as a 6GHz-anchored MLO capacity play
wireless.recommended_action: Enable OFDMA + BSS-Coloring for dense low-rate populations, reserve MU-MIMO for high-rate clients, apply TWT to IoT/battery; anchor Wi-Fi 7 value in 6GHz with MLO for latency/reliability-critical SSIDs and 320MHz only where spectrum + clients allow.
wireless.citation: IEEE 802.11ax / 802.11be + Cisco/Meraki Wi-Fi 6E/7 design; web-verified (Wi-Fi 7 MLO/320MHz/4K-QAM).

dimensions.current: 23 inventoried / 23 collected device(s); roles access:19, distribution:4; 3 VLAN(s) span >= 8 switches; multiple VRFs.
dimensions.target: (needs growth horizon) -- collapsed-core vs 3-tier vs spine-leaf is a scale/growth CHOICE
dimensions.rationale: Collapsed core suits a small, single-site, low-growth footprint; a dedicated core / 3-tier earns its cost past ~3 distribution blocks or multi-building growth; spine-leaf (VXLAN-EVPN) for east-west DC scale. The L1-L4 evidence shows current scale, not the growth intent.

dimensions.current: 23 inventoried / 23 collected device(s); roles access:19, distribution:4; 3 VLAN(s) span >= 8 switches; multiple VRFs.
dimensions.target: (needs fabric_operating_model) -- Cisco ACI (APIC-controlled, application-centric EPG/contract policy fabric) vs standalone NX-OS VXLAN BGP-EVPN (controller-less, Nexus Dashboard/NDFC-managed). Both realise the same spine-leaf + distributed-anycast-gateway VXLAN outcome; the difference is the OPERATING MODEL.
dimensions.rationale: A top-down operating-model decision, not a brownfield observable: default to NX-OS VXLAN-EVPN for new builds (open RFC 7432/8365 standards, portable multivendor skills, Nexus Dashboard/NDFC ops incl. IP Fabric for Media) unless an existing ACI estate or an application-centric end-to-end identity micro-segmentation mandate justifies ACI's single declarative policy controller. Supply fabric_operating_model to resolve it.

dimensions.current: 3 oversized bridging domain(s); 5 VLAN(s) in multiple VRFs.
dimensions.target: Push the L3 boundary toward the edge (routed access, or a per-block distribution SVI) and confine each VLAN to one access switch/block; in the target VXLAN-EVPN fabric, Layer-2 is bounded to the leaf edge with a BGP-EVPN control plane (control-plane MAC/IP learning, not flood-and-learn); segment into VRFs/zones so a broadcast or STP event stays local.
dimensions.rationale: A transparently-bridged VLAN is one failure domain; bounding its span limits blast radius and improves convergence and scale.

dimensions.current: 1 single-gateway VLAN(s) (per-VLAN SPOF) + 0 multi-gateway VLAN(s) without FHRP (no VIP failover) = 1 gateway VLAN(s) lacking full first-hop redundancy.
dimensions.target: Provide first-hop redundancy: in a classic distribution, dual gateways with FHRP (HSRP/VRRP) and the STP root co-located with the active gateway; in the target VXLAN-EVPN fabric, a DISTRIBUTED ANYCAST GATEWAY -- the same gateway IP/MAC on every leaf, so first-hop routing is local at the ingress leaf and survives any single node (the EVPN replacement for centralized FHRP, seamless on host mobility).
dimensions.rationale: First-hop redundancy is structural HA; a single gateway is a per-VLAN single point of failure.

dimensions.target: Replace the 5 past-LDoS asset(s); plan refresh for the 1 approaching LDoS; carry ~18 supportable asset(s) forward; collect the 0 un-assessed device(s) before finalising -- do not design resilience on unseen gear.
dimensions.rationale: The target fabric must not inherit end-of-support hardware; coverage gaps are unknowns, not health.

dimensions.current: 2 move-group(s) (largest is a 19-switch L2-coupled group) across 23 switch(es).
dimensions.target: Phased build-before-break in 1 candidate wave(s) of <= 40 switches (0 oversized group(s) sliced into sequenced sub-waves, the rest batched); stand the target up in parallel, validate (NRFU) per wave, cut over, then decommission -- preserving rollback at each wave. Bridge legacy<->fabric with a SINGLE logical L2 link per VLAN (the EVPN fabric does not forward STP BPDUs) and move each VLAN's default gateway to the fabric anycast gateway once its endpoints are migrated, then shut the legacy SVI.
dimensions.rationale: A parallel target with right-sized, per-wave-validated waves beats both a big-bang cutover and an unmanageable single 251-switch 'wave'.

replacement_bom.note: Quantities are the current models at/near end-of-support; a supported successor SKU is selected at detailed design (not auto-chosen here). Supportable assets carry forward.

segmentation_plan.target: Segment into security zones aligned to a data classification (which assets must be isolated from which); supply data_classification to propose the VLAN->zone map -- zones are not assumed here.

addressing_plan.note: Supply an address_space (supernet, e.g. 10.0.0.0/16) to allocate target subnets; a net-new IP plan is not fabricated without one.

wave_plan.note: Candidate migration waves (<= 40 switches each). 'coupled-subwave' = a slice of one oversized L2-coupled move-group -- these share VLANs, so they are a SEQUENCE and the shared VLANs must be extended/coordinated across sub-waves until the group fully migrates. 'independent-batch' = unrelated small groups packed together (parallelizable). The full per-wave member switch lists and ordered cutover steps are in the per-wave MOP (one section per candidate wave).

aci_move_groups.note: 3 ACI tenant move-group(s), 3 EPG(s) total -- migrate tenant by tenant (the ACI policy boundary); each tenant's EPGs are the finest move unit. Tenants flagged with an unenforced VRF carry a segmentation gap to close in the target design before the move.

coverage.caveat: Design decisions are grounded only in collected evidence; not-collected devices (including any uncollected core) are an explicit unknown -- their role and redundancy are not assumed.

summary.headline: Candidate target-state across 6 dimension(s); 2 await a requirement -- a proposal to validate, not a final design.

target_state.scope_note: Architecture + LLD detail (tier model, L2/L3 boundary, resilience, lifecycle disposition + replacement BoM, target segmentation, net-new IP plan, migration). The IP plan and zone map are requirement-gated (address_space / data_classification) so nothing is fabricated; supply those to firm them up.

evpn_migration.model_basis: engine-default — NX-OS VXLAN-EVPN assumed; supply fabric_operating_model to confirm
evpn_migration.summary: 5 EVPN-migration guardrail(s) (3 High/Critical) — target fabric engine-default — NX-OS VXLAN-EVPN assumed; supply fabric_operating_model to confirm.

guardrails.title: NX-OS 10.2(3) HSRP↔Anycast-Gateway coexistence gate
guardrails.basis: all 1 NX-OS device(s) parsed at or above 10.2(3) (re-verify the fabric-border nodes)
guardrails.detail: Before NX-OS 10.2(3) a switch CANNOT run a legacy FHRP/HSRP gateway and the fabric Distributed Anycast Gateway for the SAME subnet at once. Any node that must hold both during seamless coexistence (the border/anchor leaf, and any legacy device keeping its gateway through transition) needs NX-OS >= 10.2(3); otherwise keep the default gateway in the legacy network until the subnet's workloads have fully migrated, or move the gateway to the fabric first. Verify the running train on BOTH the legacy and the fabric-border nodes.
guardrails.source: Cisco NX-OS VXLAN Config Guide 'Default Gateway Coexistence of HSRP and Anycast Gateway'; BRKDCN-2951

guardrails.title: First-hop gateway / virtual-MAC transition (mandatory pre-step)
guardrails.basis: 8 of 9 gateway(s) run FHRP/HSRP — their virtual MAC must be aligned to the DAG MAC
guardrails.detail: In a maintenance window, BEFORE any workload moves, reconfigure each legacy HSRP virtual MAC to MATCH the fabric Distributed-Anycast-Gateway MAC (e.g. 2020.0000.00aa), then force hosts to refresh their ARP cache by failing the HSRP standby to active (gratuitous ARP). Not all hosts honour GARP (static entries / GARP-ignoring stacks need a manual ARP flush) — a vMAC mismatch at cutover black-holes the subnet until ARP caches expire.
guardrails.source: BRKDCN-2951 (2025); Cisco 'Migrating Classic Ethernet to VXLAN BGP EVPN' white paper

guardrails.title: Exactly ONE active L2 interconnect (the overlay will NOT break a loop)
guardrails.basis: 0 vPC domain(s); STP present on 19 device(s) in the brownfield
guardrails.detail: The VXLAN overlay neither forwards nor blocks STP BPDUs, so loop protection across the legacy↔fabric boundary is NOT automatic. Permit exactly ONE active Layer-2 connection between the brownfield and the new fabric — a double-sided vPC (vPC+ for a FabricPath brownfield) at the L2/L3 demarcation that keeps all links forwarding with no loop. Keep the classic network as the STP root, BPDU-filter the interconnect, and decommission the L2 interconnect once it is no longer needed.
guardrails.source: Cisco 'Migrating Classic Ethernet / FabricPath to VXLAN BGP EVPN' white papers; BRKDCN-2951

guardrails.title: vPC back-to-back coexistence (the documented seamless-migration method)
guardrails.basis: no vPC pair observed — a vPC pair (any fabric VTEP pair) is required for the L2 interconnect
guardrails.detail: Cisco's documented method for seamless workload migration: (1) deploy the VXLAN BGP-EVPN fabric alongside the legacy network; (2) build BOTH a Layer-2 and a Layer-3 interconnect at the legacy L2/L3 demarcation via a double-sided vPC; (3) migrate workloads — traffic between migrated and not-yet-migrated endpoints traverses the step-2 interconnects during transition. (A non-seamless per-VLAN/subnet approach and EVPN Multi-Site / VRF-lite handoffs are documented alternatives.)
guardrails.source: BRKDCN-2951 (2025); Cisco classic-Ethernet / FabricPath migration white papers

guardrails.title: Rollback triggers (abort conditions for a migrated subnet/wave)
guardrails.basis: the step-2 L2+L3 interconnect remains in place until the wave is accepted, enabling per-subnet rollback
guardrails.detail: Abort the wave and move the affected subnet's gateway + VLAN back to the legacy network (across the still-present interconnect) if ANY of: a gateway-MAC mismatch black-holes a migrated subnet (host ARP not refreshed); a Layer-2 loop forms (the overlay will not break it); the EVPN control plane (underlay IGP or iBGP-EVPN) is not Established on a migrated leg; or post-cutover reachability / NRFU fails.
guardrails.source: derived from the documented loop / gateway-MAC / control-plane failure modes (migration white papers)

evpn_acceptance.title: NX-OS 10.2(3) HSRP↔Anycast-Gateway coexistence gate
evpn_acceptance.description: Before NX-OS 10.2(3) a switch CANNOT run a legacy FHRP/HSRP gateway and the fabric Distributed Anycast Gateway for the SAME subnet at once. Any node that must hold both during seamless coexistence (the border/anchor leaf, and any legacy device keeping its gateway through transition) needs NX-OS >= 10.2(3); otherwise keep the default gateway in the legacy network until the subnet's workloads have fully migrated, or move the gateway to the fabric first. Verify the running train on BOTH the legacy and the fabric-border nodes.
evpn_acceptance.pass_criteria: Verify: all 1 NX-OS device(s) parsed at or above 10.2(3) (re-verify the fabric-border nodes)
evpn_acceptance.principle_citation: Cisco NX-OS VXLAN Config Guide 'Default Gateway Coexistence of HSRP and Anycast Gateway'; BRKDCN-2951

evpn_acceptance.title: First-hop gateway / virtual-MAC transition (mandatory pre-step)
evpn_acceptance.description: In a maintenance window, BEFORE any workload moves, reconfigure each legacy HSRP virtual MAC to MATCH the fabric Distributed-Anycast-Gateway MAC (e.g. 2020.0000.00aa), then force hosts to refresh their ARP cache by failing the HSRP standby to active (gratuitous ARP). Not all hosts honour GARP (static entries / GARP-ignoring stacks need a manual ARP flush) — a vMAC mismatch at cutover black-holes the subnet until ARP caches expire.
evpn_acceptance.pass_criteria: Verify: 8 of 9 gateway(s) run FHRP/HSRP — their virtual MAC must be aligned to the DAG MAC
evpn_acceptance.principle_citation: BRKDCN-2951 (2025); Cisco 'Migrating Classic Ethernet to VXLAN BGP EVPN' white paper

evpn_acceptance.title: Exactly ONE active L2 interconnect (the overlay will NOT break a loop)
evpn_acceptance.description: The VXLAN overlay neither forwards nor blocks STP BPDUs, so loop protection across the legacy↔fabric boundary is NOT automatic. Permit exactly ONE active Layer-2 connection between the brownfield and the new fabric — a double-sided vPC (vPC+ for a FabricPath brownfield) at the L2/L3 demarcation that keeps all links forwarding with no loop. Keep the classic network as the STP root, BPDU-filter the interconnect, and decommission the L2 interconnect once it is no longer needed.
evpn_acceptance.pass_criteria: Verify: 0 vPC domain(s); STP present on 19 device(s) in the brownfield
evpn_acceptance.principle_citation: Cisco 'Migrating Classic Ethernet / FabricPath to VXLAN BGP EVPN' white papers; BRKDCN-2951

evpn_acceptance.title: vPC back-to-back coexistence (the documented seamless-migration method)
evpn_acceptance.description: Cisco's documented method for seamless workload migration: (1) deploy the VXLAN BGP-EVPN fabric alongside the legacy network; (2) build BOTH a Layer-2 and a Layer-3 interconnect at the legacy L2/L3 demarcation via a double-sided vPC; (3) migrate workloads — traffic between migrated and not-yet-migrated endpoints traverses the step-2 interconnects during transition. (A non-seamless per-VLAN/subnet approach and EVPN Multi-Site / VRF-lite handoffs are documented alternatives.)
evpn_acceptance.pass_criteria: Verify: no vPC pair observed — a vPC pair (any fabric VTEP pair) is required for the L2 interconnect
evpn_acceptance.principle_citation: BRKDCN-2951 (2025); Cisco classic-Ethernet / FabricPath migration white papers

evpn_acceptance.title: Rollback triggers (abort conditions for a migrated subnet/wave)
evpn_acceptance.description: Abort the wave and move the affected subnet's gateway + VLAN back to the legacy network (across the still-present interconnect) if ANY of: a gateway-MAC mismatch black-holes a migrated subnet (host ARP not refreshed); a Layer-2 loop forms (the overlay will not break it); the EVPN control plane (underlay IGP or iBGP-EVPN) is not Established on a migrated leg; or post-cutover reachability / NRFU fails.
evpn_acceptance.pass_criteria: Verify: the step-2 L2+L3 interconnect remains in place until the wave is accepted, enabling per-subnet rollback
evpn_acceptance.principle_citation: derived from the documented loop / gateway-MAC / control-plane failure modes (migration white papers)

design_nrfu.note: Design-driven NRFU/ATP checklist: 60 acceptance-test item(s), one per recommended design decision, each traceable to the CCDE principle and the evidence that triggered it. Run after each migration wave; the pass/fail verdict for each item is independent of the design authors (proposer ≠ verifier). Items phased: pre-cutover → post-cutover-functional → post-cutover-operational.
